jobs.title: Territory Manager (Oklahoma)
jobs.description:
ABOUT HALTER

At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional practices. Imagine watching 500 cattle stand up and walk calmly towards their next break? No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences. Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance. Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard. 

We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund https://foundersfund.com, Bessemer Venture Partners https://www.bvp.com/, BOND, https://www.bondcap.com/ DCVC https://www.dcvc.com/, Blackbird https://www.blackbird.vc/, Promus Ventures https://www.promusventures.com/, Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures https://www.icehouseventures.co.nz/?utm_term=icehouse%20ventures&utm_campaign=Brand+Keywords&utm_source=adwords&utm_medium=ppc&hsa_acc=4064636360&hsa_cam=16902737884&hsa_grp=134004309485&hsa_ad=592971340272&hsa_src=g&hsa_tgt=kwd-1082530126230&hsa_kw=icehouse%20ventures&hsa_mt=b&hsa_net=adwords&hsa_ver=3&gclid=Cj0KCQjw2v-gBhC1ARIsAOQdKY0J0DepRVFDmjQlAkJPbZuQnLSA5UVzUzOXYiPxkjX-SeVa513_BhkaAr-MEALw_wcB.

To find out more, visit our LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/halter-limited & Instagram https://www.instagram.com/lifeathalter/.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Ever dream about being in tech but aren’t quite ready to trade in your cowboy boots? Look no further than Halter! As the leading provider of virtual fencing technology, Halter is on a mission to enable 50% of the world’s landmass to be more productive and sustainable. This role is paramount for our growth aspirations and will enable us to continue making an impact on ranches across the US.

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving new business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction. In this role, you will prioritize daily efforts that optimize performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and Customer Onboarding, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of US farmers.

Your day-to-day could include being on horseback, helping customers gather their cattle, on a side-by-side traversing their pastures, talking about how Halter could benefit their pastures, or attending industry events like CattleCon or your local Livestock Association meetups.



This role covers the North West Panhandle region of Oklahoma. Frequent travel is required as apart of this role.




WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Prospecting New Business: You’re driving up driveways, attending local cattle auctions, meeting with your local Livestock, Cattleman's, Stockman's associations, building your new business pipeline through outbound lead generation efforts. You’re fielding inbound leads in a timely manner, prioritizing administrative tasks with your in-field activities.

 - In-Field Sales: You don’t mind getting your hands and boots dirty. Halter is best discussed over a coffee at a kitchen table, in the horse saddle, or on a side-by-side in a pasture. You’re out on the ranch helping potential customers before diving into the value of Halter. You’re dropping off coffee during calving season. You value the magic moments that make all the difference to our customers.

 - Expanding Existing Opportunities: You’re always looking for new opportunities, and that includes expanding your existing customers with Halter. You find value in expanding relationships and finding new ways to increase value over time. Not every rancher will collar all of their cows, so you see this as a unique opportunity to meet your goals.

 - Hitting Sales Targets: High-growth sales targets don’t scare you; you step up to a challenge and like shooting high. You’re an expert pipeline manager and don’t second-guess unqualifying a lead. You’re able to manage today’s deals while keeping next month in your sights.

 - Customer Account Management: Building relationships is more than just making the sale to you. After the sale, you aim to maintain close relationships with your customers to ensure their ongoing satisfaction, provide support, and address any challenges they face with Halter’s products. You’ll also ensure a smooth handoff from sales to customer onboarding and deployment of Halter, helping customers get the most value from Halter’s solutions.

 - Territory Ownership: You have a high level of ownership and take pride in what you build. Owning an entire territory means giving treatment to every corner and leaving no stone unturned. You value being the face of your territory, meeting with high-level stakeholders from various local, state, and federal agencies to build lasting relationships with regional agricultural groups.

 - Customer Onboarding: Your high level of ownership doesn’t stop after the sale. You dive in to make sure your customers have the very best onboarding experience possible. You actively own the end-to-end customer experience during onboarding and deployment of Halter’s product, ensuring a smooth transition from sales to implementation even when you’ve handed off the customer to different teams across Halter.

 - Field Learnings & Feedback: Feedback is not only paramount to the companies you want to work for, but it’s also ingrained in how you would own your territory. Serving as the primary point of contact for gathering customer feedback in your territory, you work tirelessly to advocate for what your customers need.

 - Collaborating with Support Teams: You’re a natural collaborator, seeking out partners across Halter to resolve any issues your customers encounter, and quickly. You escalate problems as needed and ensure that customers in your territory feel fully supported.

 - Attending Industry Events: You leverage opportunities at relevant industry and Halter events to generate leads and deepen relationships with existing customers. You’ll participate in demonstrations and network to expand Halter’s influence in the market.

 - Contributing to the US Sales Strategy: You strongly believe that a team can only be stronger when they work together. You strive to work with the broader team to optimize and evolve the sales process, ensuring it fits the US market. As we scale, your input will help drive greater efficiencies.



YOU’LL BE GREAT IF YOU EXHIBIT

 - Driven Attitude & Communication skills: Results-driven, motivated, and adaptable, you excel in high-stakes environments. You’re well-prepared and skilled at communicating with customers and internal teams alike. You are proactive and do not wait to act.

 - Ranching / Cattle Experience: You know the ropes (and the reins) of ranching or cattle operations, understanding the unique challenges of the industry. This experience allows you to connect meaningfully with customers about what matters most.

 - Sales & Customer Success Expertise: You have a strong history of creating new business opportunities, negotiating a value-based sales conversation, and have a background in building lasting customer relationships. You build relationships versus transactional sales, aiming for the long-term success stories and can expand existing relationships through upsell opportunities.

 - Territory Management experience: Experience managing a large territory with a balanced focus on sales and customer success, ideally within agriculture or technology.

 - Problem Solving & Collaboration ability: Resourceful and quick-thinking, you work well with cross-functional teams to address challenges and drive solutions.

 - Willingness to Travel: Frequent travel within your territory to engage with customers and prospects.



BONUS THINGS YOU COULD BRING ALONG TO THE ROLE

 - Familiarity with precision agriculture or virtual fencing technologies.

 - Background in customer-facing roles within agriculture technology.

 - Background in selling software (SaaS) solutions in a B2B environment.



OUR BENEFITS

 - Our personal growth is important. Halter offers an annual USD$750 self-development budget to be used for anything that fuels personal growth.

 - Health Benefits - We offer best-in-class insurance for our employees, so they can care for themselves and their families.

 - 16 weeks of paid parental leave for primary and 8 weeks for secondary caregivers plus many other parental benefits that support you and your family.

 - Our time to recharge is valued, we’re offered wellness leave and unlimited paid annual leave.

 - We're proud to offer 401k and make an employer match. We offer a 100% match on the first 3% you contribute, and a 50% match on the next 2%.

 - Importantly, we offer an inclusive and attractive remuneration package made up of salary, benefits and an employee stock ownership plan.


JOIN OUR TEAM

Halter is committed to promoting a diverse and inclusive workplace — a place where we can each be ourselves and do the best work of our lives. Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the requirements, women and under-represented groups of candidates tend to only apply when they meet every requirement. If you think you have what it takes but don’t necessarily tick every requirement on this job description, please still get in touch and apply to Halter. We’d love to chat to see if you’ll be an epic fit!

If this opportunity sounds like you, please apply below by sending through your cover letter explaining why you’re excited about this role and working at Halter, along with your CV, and we’ll be in touch!

Please also feel free to check out the careers page https://www.halterhq.com/careers for more information on working at Halter and don't forget to follow us on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/halter-limited & Instagram https://www.instagram.com/lifeathalter/.




WHY OUR TEAM LOVES WORKING AT HALTER:

 - Work that genuinely matters. Every now and again a company comes along that transforms an entire industry and leaves the world in a better place. Our team gets to be part of something truly meaningful, helping farmers improve their livelihoods, spend more time with their families, and build more sustainable operations.

 - Spectacular people solving hard problems. Our culture is designed for talented people to do work that changes lives. The team is filled with diverse, kind, and driven people who push each other to do their best work. You'll be thrown into the deep end, tackling complex challenges and building something tangible that solves real problems.

 - You'll grow here. Autonomy, mastery, and learning define how we work. You'll have the freedom to work on interesting problems, master new skills, and continuously develop yourself, both through your role and our personal growth fund.

 - This isn't easy, and we love that it's hard. Working at Halter will be the most rewarding and the most challenging work of your life. We move fast, take bold bets, and work hard to reshape an entire industry. As one team member put it: "Joining Halter is a bit like strapping yourself to a rocket ship, but it's an epic journey to be a part of!"

Responsibilities:

• Prepares exam rooms for patient use by cleaning the rooms between patients and ensuring that each room is stocked with the appropriate supplies. Prepares procedure trays as necessary.

• Assists physicians and other providers with patient procedures such as suture removal, wart and mole removal, minor surgeries, etc.

• Prepares specimens to be analyzed by an outside lab by packaging specimen appropriately, completing requisition form and contacting testing facility as necessary. Submits lab results to physician before contacting patient and filing patient's chart

• Facilitates referrals to other physicians by phoning their offices, making an appointment for the patient, and forwarding requested test results, etc.

• Contacts Hospital and outside sources regarding lab results, x‑ray results and ER reports; phones pharmacies to authorize prescriptions; contacts nursing homes regarding patient orders; contacts patients to relay test result information; and returns patients phone calls with the physician's recommendations for their care.

• Pre‑certifies medications and referrals by contacting the appropriate insurance professionals and providing them with the requested information. Records pre‑certification number in chart. Records and tracks all referrals.

job purpose:

The Procurement Manager, Paper (corrugate) & Flex (shrink sleeves, shrink film, stretch film) Packaging is accountable for leading all activities within strategic sourcing and procurement operations for the Paper and Flex categories within the packaging portfolio at fairlife. This role is directly responsible for managing and overseeing the development and execution of sourcing strategies that align with fairlife’s strategic objectives: cost improvements, supply resilience, innovation, and supporting growth. responsibilities:

jobs.title: Regional Director ICF Operations
jobs.description:
As Dungarvin’s Regional Director, you will serve as a senior operational executive leading a multi-state region across Louisiana, Texas, Oklahoma, and New Mexico. You will drive quality outcomes, financial performance, regulatory excellence, leadership development, and strategic growth across a diverse portfolio of services supporting individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

This high-impact role oversees a $50M+ operation supporting approximately 700 employees across residential services, ICF/IID, day programs, employment services, and community-based supports. As a key partner to the COO and executive team, you will shape regional strategy, support growth and acquisition initiatives, navigate complex operational challenges, and develop high-performing leaders.

This is an opportunity for a strategic, mission-driven executive to influence the future of a growing region while making a meaningful impact on the individuals and communities we serve.

What You Get To Do:

• Lead Multi-State Regional Operations: Provide executive oversight for Louisiana, Texas, Oklahoma, and New Mexico operations, ensuring high-quality, person-centered services while achieving operational, financial, and organizational goals.
• Drive Quality, Compliance & Risk Management: Strengthen quality assurance systems, monitor performance trends, ensure regulatory readiness, and proactively identify opportunities to reduce risk and improve outcomes.
• Own Financial Performance & Growth Strategy: Oversee regional financial performance, including P&L accountability, budgeting, forecasting, labor optimization, and resource allocation while identifying opportunities for sustainable growth and improved business performance.
• Lead Strategic Growth & Organizational Change: Support business development initiatives, acquisitions, change-of-ownership activities, integration efforts, and strategic projects that expand services and strengthen regional operations.
• Develop High-Performing Leaders: Coach, mentor, and develop senior leaders while building leadership pipelines, strengthening accountability, and fostering a culture aligned with Dungarvin’s mission and values.
• Build Strategic Partnerships: Establish strong relationships with internal leaders, state agencies, funding partners, regulatory organizations, families, and community stakeholders to advance organizational goals.

MUST HAVE:

• Education: Bachelor’s degree in Human Services or a related field (Psychology, Counseling, Allied Health, Educational Psychology, Sociology, etc.).
• Executive Leadership Experience: 5+ years of progressive senior-level leadership experience overseeing complex human services operations, developing leaders, managing geographically dispersed teams, and achieving quality, operational, and financial objectives.
• Human Services & ICF/IID Experience: 7+ years of experience supporting individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, including direct experience overseeing Intermediate Care Facilities (ICF/IID) and services such as residential, day programs, employment/vocational supports, and community-based programs.
• Financial & Operational Leadership: Proven experience overseeing $50M+ budgets, P&L performance, forecasting, labor management, and resource allocation while leveraging operational metrics to improve performance and support strategic decision-making.
• Strategic Growth & Change Management: Experience leading multi-state initiatives, M&A activities, change-of-ownership processes, RFPs, business development efforts, and organizational transformation initiatives.
• Technology & Data Analytics: Proficient with Microsoft 365 applications and operational reporting systems, with experience leveraging Power BI dashboards and analytics to identify trends, measure outcomes, improve performance, and drive continuous improvement.

NICE TO HAVE:

• Regulatory & Managed Care Expertise: Strong knowledge of ID/DD/IDD, ICF, HCBS, Medicaid Waiver programs, managed care models, CMS requirements, state licensing regulations, compliance standards, and quality assurance practices. Experience navigating multi-state operations, funding structures, provider networks, crisis management, and system-level change.
• Process Optimization & Change Leadership: Experience evaluating operations, improving systems and workflows, and implementing strategies that enhance service quality, operational efficiency, and organizational effectiveness.
• Professional Development & Certifications: Advanced education, leadership training, or relevant certifications such as CPHQ, PMP, cHAP, Lean Six Sigma, CARF accreditation/surveyor credentials, or other healthcare, quality, or compliance credentials.

SKILLS CRITICAL FOR SUCCESS:

• Executive Leadership & Influence: Builds trust, develops leaders, creates accountability, and effectively influences teams, executives, regulatory partners, and community stakeholders.
• Strategic Thinking & Business Acumen: Balances mission, people, quality, and financial performance while identifying opportunities, anticipating challenges, and driving sustainable growth.
• Data-Driven Decision Making: Uses KPIs, operational trends, and analytics tools such as Power BI to identify risks, improve outcomes, and guide strategic decisions.
• Communication & Relationship Building: Communicates with transparency, confidence, and diplomacy while building strong partnerships across diverse teams and stakeholder groups.
• Adaptability & Resilience: Thrives in a dynamic, travel-intensive environment by managing competing priorities, navigating ambiguity, and responding effectively to complex challenges.
• Operational Problem Solving: Identifies root causes, recognizes emerging trends, and implements sustainable solutions that improve quality, efficiency, and business performance.
• Emotional Intelligence & Mission Alignment: Demonstrates empathy, sound judgment, and discretion while maintaining accountability and ensuring decisions align with Dungarvin’s mission and values.

WHY YOU’LL LOVE THIS ROLE:

This role offers the opportunity to lead a significant, growing region while making a lasting impact on individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. You will have the autonomy to shape operations, develop future leaders, influence strategic direction, and partner with executive leadership on initiatives that support long-term organizational growth.

You will join a mission-driven organization where your leadership directly impacts quality outcomes, employee success, and the communities we serve. With visibility, ownership, and the opportunity to influence the future of regional operations, this role provides the challenge, purpose, and professional growth expected of a senior executive leader.

IMPORTANT INFORMATION:

We believe in supporting not only those we serve but also each other, ensuring a collaborative and supportive work environment for all. Recording & Resource Scheduling

• Manage a high volume of audiobook recording bookings across multiple studios and production resources across various time zones.
• Coordinate availability among narrators, authors, directors, engineers, studios, agents, producers, and other production personnel.
• Partner closely with producers to prioritize bookings and meet production deadlines.
• Respond quickly to new requests, cancellations, schedule changes, talent availability, and special production needs.

jobs.title: Supervisor, QC (Swing Shift)
jobs.description:
Swing Shift Working Hours: Monday to Friday, 3:00 PM to 11:30 PM PT.

Position Summary

The Supervisor, Quality Control oversees the Quality Control Chemistry Laboratory and Oligonucleotide Quality Control Analytics Laboratory, supporting high-throughput oligonucleotide testing and production activities within regulated quality systems. The role provides strategic team leadership, coordinates priorities across Quality Control, Manufacturing, Research and Development, and Quality, and drives operational consistency across laboratory teams. This people-management role develops staff, plans capacity and cross-training, and supports resource allocation, investigations, and continuous improvement. The position requires strong analytical, organizational, leadership, and communication skills in a fast-paced laboratory environment.

Primary Duties

• Provide leadership and operational oversight for multiple Quality Control laboratory teams and functional areas
• Assign work, establish priorities, train and mentor staff, support recruiting and succession planning, and evaluate team performance
• Develop and implement mid-term capacity, cross-training, and resource-allocation strategies that align testing activities with production needs
• Oversee analytical testing of chemical products and oligonucleotides using high-performance liquid chromatography, liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry, spectrophotometry, DNA synthesizers, and related laboratory equipment
• Review analytical results against specifications and customer requirements and support product-disposition recommendations
• Oversee investigations, deviation support, risk assessments, technical decisions, and summary reporting with broader impact across Quality Control operations
• Ensure compliant documentation and testing practices under applicable Good Documentation Practice, Good Manufacturing Practice, ISO 9001, and ISO 13485 requirements
• Partner with Manufacturing, Research and Development, Quality, and internal customers to align testing schedules, deadlines, results, and quality expectations
• Author, review, and maintain standard operating procedures, work instructions, safety documentation, and Quality Control records
• Identify and implement process improvements that strengthen safety, efficiency, documentation accuracy, laboratory organization, and operational performance
• Ensure safe handling, labeling, storage, and disposal of samples, reagents, hazardous materials, and waste in accordance with training and policy
• Perform other duties as required or assigned by management to meet business needs

Work Conditions and Environment

• Travel & Time Expectations: Periodic travel to customer, vendor, or company sites as needed to support the business, less than 20%
• Work Setting: Primarily a laboratory and office environment with regular exposure to manufacturing areas and moderate to loud noise levels
• Distinctive Safety Conditions: Potential exposure to hazardous chemicals, materials, and waste requiring adherence to safety precautions, chemical-handling practices, and required training
• Required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): Laboratory coat, gloves, goggles, closed-toe non-slip shoes, and other personal protective equipment as required by policy and task

Knowledge, Experience, Skills, and Certifications

Essential Knowledge and Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Analytical Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biology, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related field
• Hands-on laboratory experience in a regulated Quality Control environment with demonstrated ability to lead laboratory priorities and staff
• Working knowledge of analytical testing for chemical products and oligonucleotides
• Proficiency operating, maintaining, and troubleshooting relevant laboratory equipment, including high-performance liquid chromatography, liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry, spectrophotometers, DNA synthesizers, and pH meters
• Knowledge of ISO 9001, ISO 13485, Good Manufacturing Practice, Good Documentation Practice, and quality documentation expectations applicable to laboratory testing
• Ability to review analytical results against specifications and customer requirements and support scientifically sound technical decisions
• Experience supporting investigations, deviations, risk assessments, process improvements, and technical summary reports
• Knowledge of hazardous chemical handling, laboratory safety, personal protective equipment, waste management, and applicable compliance practices
• Demonstrated ability to schedule and prioritize analytical work, manage multiple tasks, and communicate deadlines and results to stakeholders
• Demonstrated ability to train, mentor, and develop Quality Control staff while promoting consistency, accountability, and safe work practices

Desired Knowledge and Qualifications

• Advanced experience with high-performance liquid chromatography and Quality Control testing in an industry laboratory
• Proficiency with laboratory and business software such as FileMaker Pro, MassLynx, Empower, IFS, and Microsoft Office

• Proven success in mentoring, project management, succession planning, and continuous improvement

jobs.title: Product Marketing Lead:  Temp Maternity Leave Coverage
jobs.description:
About Faire

Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.

We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.

About this role

Product Marketing at Faire is a strategic function embedded across the product lifecycle. PMMs partner closely with Product, Design, Marketing, and Revenue to shape programs from the ground up, develop positioning and messaging, lead GTM strategy, and drive awareness and adoption. We have PMMs focused on each side of the marketplace: the brands who sell on Faire, and the retailers who buy from them.

We're looking for a senior product marketer we'd trust with any area we prioritize. You'll be the marketing owner for your product area: you set the GTM strategy, make the calls, and deliver it, working as a peer with a senior cross-functional and executive team. You find new opportunities rather than waiting to be handed them, bring approaches we haven't tried, make complex products feel simple, and influence how the product itself evolves. You move comfortably between strategy and execution, at pace, and your scope may shift during the engagement as the business’s needs change.

Set direction and own the area

• Find new opportunities in your area and lead them from concept through implementation. Set the strategy rather than executing someone else's brief.

• Own end-to-end GTM for your area, from positioning through launch and adoption, and influence the long-term GTM direction with cross-functional leaders.

• Introduce approaches not yet tried at Faire to solve open-ended problems, and influence how decisions get made across cross-functional teams.

Positioning and narrative

• Develop deep customer understanding and translate it into clear, compelling positioning

• Make Faire feel simple to customers. Cut jargon, kill messaging that doesn't matter, and push back on product complexity that won't land.

• Build positioning from scratch and reposition existing products so they land with new or shifting audiences.

• Develop messaging narratives and personas that connect multiple products into one coherent story, driving long-term engagement and retention rather than one-off launch messaging.

GTM and adoption

• Guide cross-functional GTM teams to operationalize complex, multi-channel campaigns, sequencing customer engagement and education to drive behavior change at the right moments.

• Drive adoption through the right motion for your area, whether sales-assisted or lifecycle-driven: equip sales teams to pitch and close, and build lifecycle and CRM comms that move customers from awareness to adoption to retention.

• Ship to learn: Make directionally right calls with ~70% of the information, put things in market, and iterate fast rather than waiting for perfect.

• Coordinate enablement across Revenue, CX, Lifecycle, and other partners to bring GTM plans to life.

Influence, measurement, and craft

• Shape product roadmaps and program design upstream through customer insight, acting as a customer-centric thought partner to Product, Design, Legal, and other stakeholders.

• Communicate with clarity and credibility at the executive level, and use narratives, positioning docs, data, and insights to align senior stakeholders behind a direction.

• Build the business case and establish clear ROI for your GTM bets, including post-mortems and optimizations, and uplevel project-level goals into a customer-level north star that connects back to business goals.

• Use AI tools to sharpen and accelerate your work, and leverage AI to elevate PMM craft at Faire.

• Raise the craft bar on the team. Give direct feedback to other PMMs and document your work so the team can carry it forward after the engagement.

Qualifications

Required

• 10+ years in product marketing or closely related GTM roles, including 6+ in core PMM, owning the GTM strategy for a product area end to end, setting direction, finding opportunities others haven't named, and leading them from concept through outcomes.

• Builds positioning from scratch, repositions existing products, and holds a coherent narrative across multiple launches rather than siloed product stories.

• Experience driving adoption through a sales-assisted or lifecycle-driven motion: enabling sales teams to pitch and close, and/or building lifecycle and CRM comms.

• Sets measurable GTM goals, architects incrementality and A/B testing with analytics partners, and builds the business case and ROI for the work. Fluent in the metrics that move the business.

• A bias to action and fast iteration: ships to learn, sets their own deadlines and beats them, and stays flexible as new information comes in.

• Experience influencing product roadmaps and program design upstream, not just executing at launch.

• Communicates and aligns senior stakeholders at the executive level.

• Experience conducting or directing customer research and translating findings into positioning and strategy.

• Experience building thematic campaigns across product areas, not just siloed launches.

• Actively experiments with and adopts AI tools to sharpen and accelerate their work, and helps the team find real ways to use AI in PMM craft.

Nice to have

• Experience working as a contractor or consultant: ramps quickly with limited onboarding and delivers independently against a defined scope.

• Background in STEM, management consulting, finance, or other quantitative fields.

• Experience in high-growth or scaling environments where PMM infrastructure was still being built.

• Experience marketing complex or highly technical products where customer trust and education are central to adoption.

• Familiarity with how independent retailers or small business owners make decisions and what earns their trust.

• Two-sided marketplace background, where brand and buyer motions are distinct but interdependent.

Salary Range

San Francisco : the pay range for this role is $180,000 to $247,500 per year.

This role will also be eligible for equity and benefits. Actual base pay will be determined based on permissible factors such as transferable skills, work experience, market demands, and primary work location. The base pay range provided is subject to change and may be modified in the future.

Hybrid Faire employees currently go into the office 3 days per week on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and a third flex day of their choosing (Monday, Wednesday, or Friday). Additionally, hybrid in-office roles will have the flexibility to work remotely up to 4 weeks per year. Specific Workplace and Information Technology positions may require onsite attendance 5 days per week as will be indicated in the job posting.

Why you’ll love working at Faire

• Move fast: You'll own meaningful problems that serve customers around the globe with the agency to move fast and see your results clearly.

• Equipped to scale: We invest in what matters, including the latest enterprise AI tools, to help you work smarter and get more out of every day.

• Best in class: Our team is full of sharp, kind, and generous colleagues who care about their craft and about helping you grow in yours.

• Real rewards. Competitive pay, equity, and comprehensive benefits designed to support your life inside and outside of work.

• Belonging: We're intentional about building an environment where every Faire employee has equal access to opportunities, growth, and success.

Faire was founded in 2017 by a team of early product and engineering leads from Square. We’re backed by some of the top investors in retail and tech including: Y Combinator, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Forerunner Ventures, Khosla Ventures, Sequoia Capital, Founders Fund, and DST Global. We have headquarters in San Francisco and Kitchener-Waterloo, and a global employee presence across offices in Toronto, London, and New York. To learn more about Faire and our customers, you can read more on our blog.

jobs.title: Executive Assistant to the CEO
jobs.description:
About Collectively:

Collectively - part of the Brandtech Group (formerly You & Mr. Jones) -  is the global leader in influencer marketing; combining strategy, creative, and technology to deliver the most innovative influencer work. We partner with forward-thinking brands in technology, fashion, retail, gaming, entertainment, consumer goods, and more to build deeply integrated social activation strategies that drive relevance, awareness, and sales. Our work has been recognized by top publications including The Wall Street Journal, Fast Company, Digiday, AdAge, and Business INSIDER, among others. We’ve also earned Effie, Webby, Glossy, IMA Fast Company, and OMMA awards for our programs.

Collectively is known across the industry as the partner who delivers the most creative, strategic, and effective programs, with the most sophisticated analysis and paid social offerings. But most importantly, we’re known to be genuinely committed partners to our clients, many of whom have worked with us for multiple years. We aspire to continue to provide an excellent workplace for our teams while delivering the industry’s most ambitious and thoughtful influencer collaborations.

About the Role

We're hiring an Executive Assistant to work closely with the CEO. The CEO works with clients, our leadership team, and the Brandtech, and this role helps keep all of that organized and moving.

Day to day, you’ll manage the CEO’s calendar, inbox, and travel. You’ll prepare them for important meetings, track decisions, and follow up so the CEO stays ahead of priorities. Each week, there will be an opportunity either virtually or in person in San Francisco to collaborate on what's ahead and adjust priorities as they change.

As you develop a deeper understanding of the business, you will have the opportunity to take on an expanded scope, and the role will evolve over time. That includes supporting the Senior Leadership Team, Brandtech meetings, internal communications, and managing select projects on the CEO's behalf.

The role is based in San Francisco and is remote-first, with regular in-person collaboration.

Responsibilities

Strategic time and calendar management

• Manage the CEO's calendar end to end, balancing internal, client, and personal commitments

• Design a daily and weekly rhythm that tackles priorities, protects deep-work blocks and solves bottlenecks

• Evaluate meeting requests and decline, delegate, or shorten where time is better spent elsewhere

• Resolve conflicts proactively and reschedules on the fly when priorities shift

Meeting preparation and follow-through

• Prepare concise briefs and agendas ahead of key meetings

• Join key meetings to capture decisions and action items, and follow up so nothing stalls

• Run a weekly planning session with the CEO to review the week ahead and adjust priorities

Travel and logistics

• Plan and book travel with efficient, well-timed itineraries

• Travel with the CEO when needed for key meetings or events

• Coordinate in-person team days and meetings in San Francisco

• Handle logistics for client dinners, pitches, gifting, and industry conferences

Communication and discretion

• Triage the CEO's inbox and flag what needs their attention

• Draft routine correspondence and scheduling communications on the CEO's behalf

• Handle confidential and personal information with complete discretion

Leadership and Staff Meetings

• Coordinate meetings with Brandtech leadership and help prepare materials in advance.

• Keep track of deadlines for recurring reporting the CEO owes to Brandtech.

• Contribute to the All Staff weekly meeting and Quarterly staff meeting by ensuring the CEO raises topics on a cyclical basis.

Administration

• Handle the CEO’s expense reports, subscriptions, and vendor coordination

• Support select personal logistics such as routinely discussing and acknowledging key milestones across her leadership team through gifting or other thoughtful gestures.

What success looks like

• First 30 days: you fully own the CEO's calendar and inbox and know the key people they work with most, both inside Collectively and across our clients and Brandtech.

• First 90 days: a consistent weekly rhythm is in place, and the CEO has reclaimed meaningful focus time each week.

• Ongoing: you anticipate scheduling needs before they arise, can contribute to key strategy projects, and you keep the CEO's time aligned with their top priorities.

Qualifications

Required

• 5+ years supporting a C-suite executive or founder in a fast-paced environment

• Expert calendar management, with sharp judgment on how to prioritize competing demands

• Based in San Francisco and available for regular in-person collaboration

• Comfortable traveling when needed

• Ability to think ahead and catch scheduling issues or preparation gaps before they arise

• Clear, polished writing, including the ability to write in someone else’s voice

• Strong project management skills, with experience keeping multiple stakeholders on track

• Comfort with frequent change, and the ability to adjust and proactively respond with solutions

• Proven discretion with confidential information

• Advanced proficiency in Slack, Google Workspace, AI-enabled note-taking tools, and Zoom

Nice to have

• Experience supporting an executive in an agency or creator-economy business

• Experience working with a parent company or board

• Familiarity with time-blocking or productivity frameworks

• Flexibility for occasional early or late calls across time zone

Benefits & Team Member Experience

• Medical, Dental & Vision

• 401k Matching

• Monthly Work From Home Stipend

• Remote-First

• Flex Fridays

• Step Up Recognition Program

• Collectively Employee Resource Groups (ERGs)

• Virtual & In-Person Events

• Generous Allotment of Sick Days

• Birthday Time Off

Pay

Collectively takes into consideration a wide range of factors that are utilized in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skill sets, experience and training, qualifications and education, and other business and organizational needs.

jobs.title: Senior Managing Consultant
jobs.description:
Technical Assent seeks a Program Manager to lead a multi-task technical and analytical support program for the Office of the Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Acquisition, Technology and Logistics (SAF/AQ). The Program Manager is accountable for all contractor work on the effort, spanning IT requirements and enterprise architecture, industrial base analysis, AI integration, acquisition program support, and the Department of the Air Force Modernized Process Model (MPM).

This is a full-time, hands-on leadership role. You will lead a multi-company team, lead the team through transition during the kick-off phase and quickly stabilize performance to ensure client objectives are met; keep every position staffed with qualified people; and serve as the primary point of contact for the Contracting Officer and COR.

About the program

SAF/AQ is the Service Acquisition Executive and Senior Procurement Executive for the Department of the Air Force. The program supports SAF/AQ, other Headquarters Air Force organizations, Program Executive Offices, Portfolio Acquisition Executives, and Department of War components. The Program Manager supervises and integrates several technical lanes, each with its own workstream lead:

• Program Management

• IT requirements, portfolio rationalization, and enterprise architecture

• Industrial base support

• Artificial intelligence support

• Strategic and acquisition support

• Acquisition integration (MPM)

Key responsibilities

Contract leadership and customer engagement

• Serve as the single point of contact for the Contracting Officer and COR, and respond to their inquiries within 24 hours during normal duty hours.

• Build trusted-advisor relationships with SAF/AQ and AQX leadership, connecting the team's work to Air Force acquisition outcomes.

• Lead strategic planning, budgeting, and staffing in response to task requirements and shifting Government priorities.

• Set, communicate, and enforce quality standards across all five lanes, and resolve issues that threaten delivery.

Leading a multi-company team

• Lead a team that includes Technical Assent employees and subcontractor personnel as one integrated workforce under Technical Assent's management.

• Direct and coordinate the five Key Personnel lanes, holding each lead accountable for quality, timeliness, and staffing.

• Flow contract performance standards down to subcontractors and manage them through regular reviews.

• Establish associate contractor agreements as directed by the Government.

Staffing and retention

• Keep every position filled with qualified, cleared personnel from contract start, and fill any vacancy within 30 days.

• Hold annual team turnover at or below 10%.

• Monitor staff performance, coach and develop analysts, and realign or replace personnel when needed, coordinating with the Government beforehand.

Financial and contract management

• Track burn rate at the CLIN/SLIN level and forecast fund depletion.

• Manage the T&M CLIN within 10% of the budget defined in the project management plan.

• Apply the approved vacancy-reduction formula and invoicing language when required.

• Track pending modifications, travel, and contract issues, and escalate to the CO as needed.

• Ensure all labor hours, including subcontractor hours, are reported in CMRA by 31 October each year.

Quality, reporting, and deliverables

Prepare and deliver:

• Quarterly Program Management Reviews, with materials due 5 business days before each briefing

• Project management plans within 10 business days of a new requirement

• The kickoff agenda and the Quality Control Plan

• Monthly Quality Control Inspection Reports

• The annual GFP list

• Run Technical Assent's quality control program so defects are identified, corrected, and prevented from recurring.

Senior Managing Consultant expectations

This role sits at Technical Assent's Senior Managing Consultant level. In this role, those expectations mean:

• Delivering client outcomes. Lead the program as one integrated effort, connecting every deliverable to SAF/AQ's mission and acquisition outcomes.

• Trusted-advisor relationships. Earn standing with SAF/AQ leadership as the person who anticipates risks and needs, not just the person who reports status.

• Integrated program management. Plan timelines, direct staff allocation across all five lanes, and run the work as a single large, complex program.

• Contribution margin. Improve the margin on the engagement by building repeatable capability in tools, technology, and talent: strong hiring pipelines, reusable templates, and efficient reporting.

• Growing the firm's expertise. Mentor the workstream leads and analysts, apply Technical Assent's consulting approaches and methods, and pursue continuous learning in DAF acquisition and related disciplines.

• Organizational capability. Build reusable process assets, templates, and tools aligned with Technical Assent's CMMI for Services (Maturity Level 3) framework, such as transition playbooks, PMR templates, and staffing trackers.

• Thought leadership. Share knowledge with internal and external peers through writing and speaking 6 to 8 times per year, subject to applicable security and public-release review.

• Account growth. Take responsibility for account goals and collaborate with Technical Assent leadership to identify growth adjacent to current work. All business development must comply with OCI restrictions, procurement integrity rules, and the contract's limits on using information obtained in performance.

• Business development lifecycle. Support capture and lead proposal or RFI responses as assigned, coordinated with leadership so contract performance and billable commitments are never compromised.

• Professional conduct. Maintain a professional demeanor consistent with Technical Assent's core values at all times.

Required qualifications

• Education: Master's degree in Business or Engineering. Experience may not be substituted for this degree.

Certification: One of the following:

• Project Management Professional (PMP)

• DAWIA Program Management Advanced, or a legacy DAWIA Level III Program Management certification

• Experience: At least 5 years managing multi-project or multi-task technical or advisory and assistance services (A&AS) contracts. The role also calls for experience leading multidisciplinary teams, managing contract financials, and serving as the primary contact for a Government CO or COR.

• Clearance: Active Secret clearance, or one eligible for reinstatement, maintained throughout performance.

• U.S. citizenship is required.

• Location: Able to work from a contractor facility within 15 miles or 30 minutes of the Pentagon, and to work regularly in person at the Pentagon and other National Capital Region Government sites.

• Availability: Able to respond to CO and COR inquiries within 24 hours during normal duty hours.

• Communication: Strong written and oral communication skills, including briefing senior Government leaders.

Preferred qualifications

• Prior Department of the Air Force acquisition service, either as an acquisition officer or as a DAF civilian program manager (GS-14/15 or equivalent).

• Direct experience with SAF/AQ or AQX and their stakeholders, including PEOs and Portfolio Acquisition Executives.

• Experience as a prime contractor's Program Manager leading a workforce that includes substantial subcontractor staff.

• Experience leading a contract transition, including knowledge capture and retention of the existing workforce.

• A track record of running cleared hiring pipelines and keeping vacancy and turnover low on staffing-sensitive contracts.

• Ownership of financial reporting on a hybrid FFP/T&M contract, including CLIN-level burn tracking and forecasting.

• Working knowledge of:

• The Adaptive Acquisition Framework and the Business Capability Acquisition Cycle (BCAC)

• Defense business system governance

• PMRT and the DAF Modernized Process Model

• Working literacy in defense industrial base and supply chain risk topics, and in AI adoption and governance within DoW frameworks.

• Both a PMP and DAWIA Program Management Advanced (or legacy Level III).

• Top Secret eligibility.

• Experience working within a CMMI for Services or similar process framework.

Work environment

• Workplace: You will work primarily from a Technical Assent facility near the Pentagon. You will spend regular time on site at the Pentagon, Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling, and other Government facilities where your team works.

• Telework: Ad hoc and situational, for unclassified work only, with COR approval.

WHAT WE OFFER

• Salary: $160,000-$200,000 annually, commensurate with skills and experience

• Comprehensive Medical, Dental & Vision coverage

• 401(k) plan with employer contributions and matching

• Company-paid Life Insurance and Short- & Long-Term Disability

• Flexible PTO

• Health & Dependent Care Spending Accounts

• OneMedical primary care membership

• Annual Learning & Development benefit to support your career growth

• Wellness benefit

• Mobile phone stipend

• Charitable contribution matching

Technical Assent is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all persons without regard to race, creed, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender identity, marital status, citizenship status, age, veteran status, or disability.

This compensation range is specific to Virginia and takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. At Technical Assent, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $160,000 to $200,000.

This position is contingent upon contract award. Final offers are contingent upon verification of education, certifications, and security clearance.

jobs.title: Senior Application Engineer – DDR5 Power Management & PMIC
jobs.description:
We are seeking an experienced and highly motivated Senior Application Engineer to join our team focusing on DDR5 solutions. In this role, you will play a critical part in driving the validation, implementation, and optimization of DDR5 memory systems, specifically focusing on digital and power efficiency. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams, to ensure that DDR5 power systems meet the highest standards of quality and reliability.

Key Responsibilities:

• Product Validation: Validation of new products within the power modules for DDR5 memory and memory controllers, ensuring compliance with industry standards and customer requirements. This includes heavy bench measurements to collect data and validate full functionality of new products.
• System-level Analysis: Conduct analysis of different DDR5 modules to identify performance and develop strategies to enhance system power efficiency without compromising performance.
• Tool Development: Create and maintain bench automation software for data collection, as well as simulation models and tools to analyze DDR5 power consumption at various system levels (e.g., chip, board, and system).
• Customer Support: Provide technical support for DDR5 power-related issues during product development and integration phases. Work directly with customers to resolve any technical issues or complex power-related challenges.
• Collaboration with Cross-functional Teams: Work closely with design, product, test, packaging and other teams to ensure DDR5 solutions meet all performance and specification requirements.
• Documentation and Reporting: Prepare technical documentation, including specifications, datasheets, power analysis reports, validation reports and test plans to support internal and external stakeholders.

• Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering (or a related field).
• Experience: 4+ years of experience in power management, memory system design, or related fields (3+ years of focus on DDR5 or similar high-speed memory technologies will be a plus).
• Skills & Expertise:Hands-on experience with bench validation of analog, digital, and power management devices (such as PMICs, SPD Hub, I3C switches, Temp sensor, etc.)Strong understanding and knowledge of analog and mixed signal circuits (such as amplifiers, temperature sensors, ADC, DAC, voltage regulators, and related power components)Automation experience using LabVIEW, Python or similar programming languagesExperience with customer support for technical design and resolving any issues at the application levelExperience with developing customer reports, Application notes, datasheets and other technical collateral
• Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to cross-functional teams and customers.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Advanced Degree: Master's or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering (or a related field).
• Additional Experience:Familiarity with DDR5 JEDEC standards and protocols is a plusExpertise in power modeling and simulation tools will be a plusExpertise in hardware design tools will be a plus

The expected annual pay range for this position is $120K-$145K. This position is also eligible for bonus opportunities. Please note that final offer amount will be dependent on geographic location, applicable experience, and skillset of the candidate.

New employees will attend a detailed benefit orientation to learn more about our many benefits and resources

jobs.title: Security Systems Technician
jobs.description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. 


We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!




HOW WE OPERATE

 - Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

 - Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

 - Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

 - Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

 - Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.




THE SECURITY TEAM

Examples of key problems the team is working on

 - You're securing the frontier of AI. The model weights training on our infrastructure are the most valuable and most targeted artifacts in technology, and we're standing up the compute to hold them faster than anyone ever has. A breach isn't a leak, it's the frontier walking out the door.

 - Build the entire security program from scratch. Most leaders inherit someone else's system and spend a career patching it. Here you own it end to end, bare metal to boardroom, as we scale across continents.

 - The industry's playbook was written for one building at a time. Vendor-managed appliances, manual process, and standards that assume a security team walks the floor. None of that survives contact with what we're building, so we build what should exist rather than buying what does.

 - Your threat surface is measured in gigawatts. The customers running on our infrastructure are building the most consequential technology in human history, and being responsible for the physical and logical security of that work makes everything else feel small.


ROLE SCOPE

 - Keep the systems online. Keep the campus's cameras, readers, door controllers, intercoms, and the head-end servers, storage and switches behind them online and reporting. Find the root cause of each failure before replacing hardware.

 - Repair on-site infrastructure. Troubleshoot and repair cable runs, failed drives, power supplies, DIMMs, NICs and optics, degraded RAID sets, and hosts that fail to boot. Keep the as-builts and device inventory current.

 - Accept new builds. Accept new data centers and expansions from the delivery team: walk down their work and the integrator's against the acceptance criteria before it enters support. Help with commissioning when the schedule requires it.

 - Work the remediation queue. Work the on-site remediation queue to the response targets in the support agreement: device swaps, firmware updates, resets, and the service requests that used to be integrator truck rolls. Escort and verify outside technicians when they are needed.

 - Keep site hardware working. Keep the hardware the guard force, GSOC and site operations use working: badge printers, visitor kiosks, turnstiles and vehicle gates.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would. https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/fluidstack/05c2e69c-42f9-4fcb-9cf0-a467aaf98f1c

 - You have maintained security devices at data center scale: cameras, readers, controllers and intercoms.

jobs.title: Fleet Support Administrator (Nashville International Airport)
jobs.description:
Are you organized, detail-oriented, and an expert in fleet management and business analysis? As a Fleet Support Administrator at SIXT, you'll play a vital role in ensuring smooth and efficient operations. You'll manage repairs, oversee work orders, and coordinate the day-to-day running of our fleet, ensuring every vehicle is ready for action. Enjoy flexible hours, endless growth opportunities, and a starting salary of $22.25 per hour.

YOUR ROLE AT SIXT

• You will ensure seamless fleet operations by performing daily inventory checks, managing vehicle availability, and coordinating with dealerships and body shops for timely repairs
• You will assist the Fleet Manager in scheduling maintenance and repairs, obtaining estimates, generating purchase orders, and organizing drivers to keep our fleet running smoothly
• You will prepare new vehicles for rental, handling tasks like adding documentation, decals, and tags, and ensuring they are added to our inventory system, ready for our customers
• You will oversee the preparation of vehicles for disposal, completing condition reports, verifying equipment, and coordinating necessary repairs
• You will monitor and track shift activities, including vehicle movements, cleaning schedules, and planning for future fleet demand, ensuring efficient and organized fleet management

YOUR SKILLS MATTER

• Analytical Skills You have strong analytical abilities and can deliver data-driven insights to improve fleet operations and have experience conducting in-depth reporting and analysis
• Organizational Skills You are highly organized, capable of managing fleet inventory, repair schedules, work orders, and documentation, ensuring efficient and smooth fleet operations across all tasks
• Team Collaboration You are a team player who thrives in a fast-paced environment and can handle multiple responsibilities
• Communication Skills You possess excellent communication skills, enabling you to work effectively with all stakeholders and deliver results
• Work Hours & Travel You can work 40 hours per week, including day or evening shifts, and are open to travel (5-10%), some of which may be by airplane
• Uniform & Language You are willing to wear a company uniform and speaking other languages is a plus

WHAT WE OFFER

• Comprehensive Benefits Package Enjoy healthcare coverage (medical, dental, vision), life insurance, critical illness, hospital indemnity, and pet insurance, along with a 401k plan to secure your future
• Paid Time Off & Holidays Benefit from PTO, sick leave, and receive time and a half for working on public holidays
• Bonus Plan Take advantage of a bonus plan based on performance
• Employee Assistance Program Access support whenever needed through our Employee Assistance Program
• Exclusive Employee Rentals Benefit from employee-only rental rates, with family rental options and exclusive discounts for employees
• Uniform & Perks Receive a uniform with weekly dry cleaning, always ensuring a professional appearance

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

About us:

We are a globally leading mobility service provider with a revenue of €4.3 billion and around 9,000 employees worldwide. Our mobility platform ONE combines our products SIXT rent (car rental), SIXT share (car sharing), SIXT ride (taxi, ride, and chauffeur services), and SIXT+ (car subscription), giving our customers access to our fleet of 360,000 vehicles, the services of 4,000 cooperation partners, and around 5 million drivers worldwide. Together with our franchise partners, we are present in more than 100 countries at 2,000 rental stations. At SIXT, top-tier customer experience and outstanding customer service are our highest priorities. We believe in true entrepreneurship and long-term stability and align our corporate strategy with foresight. Get started with us and apply now!

jobs.description:
TRAINING

The Sales Trainee (ST) is a training role.

Upon successful participation in the training program, the ST is eligible to interview for open Account Sales Manager (ASM) roles.

Upon completion of the program and certification, if no ASM or otherwise qualified role is available AND the ST is meeting performance standards, the employee may remain in the ST role up to 12-months OR until an ASM or another qualified role is available (whichever comes first).

Once an ASM or another qualified role is available, the certified ST must interview for that available role.

If promotion to the role of ACCOUNT SALES MANAGER (or other role) does not happen prior to the expiration of the 12-mos completion period, the SALES TRAINEE role will be vacated due to end of assignment unless an exception applies.

For exception, based on continued high performance, no open roles and certification completion, a manager may extend the 12-month completion period an additional 6-months.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Medical Communications
jobs.description:
Immunovant, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to enabling normal lives for people with autoimmune diseases. As trailblazers in FcRn inhibitor technology, the Company is boldly developing innovative therapies for a range of debilitating autoimmune diseases with significant unmet patient needs.

The Role:

Reporting to the Executive Director, Medical Communications & Operations, this position is responsible for managing the development of scientific content across medical communication activities.

Key Responsibilities:

• Support the development and execution of medical affairs and scientific exchange materials, including medical education, congress content, slide decks, FAQs, training materials, advisory boards and field medical tools

• Partner with medical communications agency to ensure medical materials are developed according to timelines and objectives

• Review, annotate, and proofread materials to check quality and scientific accuracy and to ensure that the content, format, and structure of documents comply with internal standards and policies and external guidelines and requirements

• Monitor deadlines and budget to ensure projects are delivered on time to align with other company-wide projects, within budget and scope

• Identify and secure copyright permission licenses, as necessary

• Participate in MRC review process, as needed

• Contribute to identifying opportunities for innovative and strategic omnichannel medical communication activities, including publication extenders, to enhance HCP engagement and scientific exchange

• Participate in congress planning activities including identifying and securing opportunities and ensuring timelines are met; partner with the clinical development and commercial teams to develop congress materials, identify training needs, and provide coverage support according to key objectives

• Support medical communications planning activities and development and pull-through of the scientific platform and narrative across channels and teams

Requirements:

• Master’s or bachelor’s level degree in science-related fields (e.g., BS, BSN, RPh, PA, NP) required; advanced degree (PharmD, M.D. or Ph.D.) preferred

• 3+ years of medical affairs experience; experience in immunology preferred

• Experience developing medical education materials required

• Experience in medical publications preferred

• Strong working knowledge of review processes and medical content compliance

• A superb command of the English language, both written and spoken; faultless grammar and spelling

• Ability to interpret complex data and articulates information across a variety of tactics

• Demonstrated ability to work with a diverse set of stakeholders on multiple projects

Work Environment:

• Remote-based

• Dynamic, interactive, fast-paced, and entrepreneurial environment

• Domestic or international travel are required (5-20%)

$160,000—$180,000 USD

• Perform certification audits in any capacity in conformance with the SGS Global/Local procedures, sector specific schemes/standards, ensure that such duties are performed in an efficient and commercially expedient way.

jobs.title: Communications Coordinator
jobs.description:
Flagship Pioneering is a scientific innovation engine that invents and builds companies that change the world. We bring together the greatest scientific minds with entrepreneurial company builders and assemble the capital to allow them to take courageous leaps in human health, sustainability, and beyond.

What sets Flagship apart is our ability to advance biotechnology by uniting life science innovation, company creation, and capital investment under one roof in a way that is largely without precedent. Our team of scientists, entrepreneurial leaders, and professional capital managers are each aligned around an institutionalized process that enables us to innovate and create breakthroughs for the benefit of people and planet.

Many of the companies Flagship has founded have addressed humanity’s most urgent challenges: vaccinating billions of people against COVID-19, curing intractable diseases, improving human health, preempting illness, and feeding the world by improving the resiliency and sustainability of agriculture.

Flagship has been recognized twice on FORTUNE’s “Change the World” list, an annual ranking of companies that have made a positive social and environmental impact through activities that are part of their core business strategies, and has been named four times to Fast Company’s annual list of the World’s Most Innovative Companies.

Position Summary:

Flagship Pioneering is seeking a highly organized, proactive Communications Coordinator to support the operations and communications efforts of its Communications & Public Affairs (CPA) team. This role will help keep a fast-moving team and its highest-priority workstreams on track—from thought leadership and company announcements to internal communications, events, and brand initiatives.

The ideal candidate is a strong project manager and communicator with excellent attention to detail, sound judgment, and an interest in science, innovation, and storytelling. They will be comfortable managing many priorities at once, coordinating across functions and external partners, and contributing to polished communications materials across formats.

Responsibilities

• Project manage key CPA workstreams, including Flagship’s Substack, The Labs Report, and its accompanying podcast, coordinating editorial development, stakeholder input, production timelines, approvals, publishing, and promotion at the direction of workstream leads and CPA leadership

• Assist the CPA team to develop and refine communications materials, including briefing documents, presentations, visual assets, newsletters, and promotional content for internal and external audiences.

• Coordinate cross-functional inputs, timelines, reviews, and approvals to help ensure communications projects move efficiently from concept through execution while flagging risks or delays to leads.

• Support planning and logistics for internal and external events, including team meetings, Town Halls, convenings, and leadership engagements.

• Help maintain team operating rhythms, including weekly meetings, project trackers, calendars, budget and billing processes, and monthly reporting.

• Coordinate vendor and agency processes, including invoice reviews, purchase order processing, contract reviews, and project-related logistics.

• Help maintain communications and brand assets so that materials are current, organized, and easy for colleagues to find and use.

• Support the management of employee headshots, biographies, and other profile materials in coordination with internal stakeholders and external vendors.

• Contribute to special projects and other communications priorities as the team and organization evolve.

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree and at least 1 year of relevant experience in communications, public relations, marketing, project management, events, or a related field.

• Strong organizational and project-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a sharp eye for detail, consistency, and quality.

• Brings creativity and strong visual instincts to the development of communications and design assets, as well as event concepts and experiences; able to help translate ideas into engaging, polished materials across channels.

• Comfort drafting and editing a range of communications materials for different audiences.

• Collaborative working style and ability to build productive relationships across teams, levels, and external partners.

• Resourceful, dependable, and comfortable working in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

• Interest in science, healthcare, technology, or innovation is strongly preferred.

Behaviors

• Thrives in ambiguity. Demonstrates comfort working in a fast-moving environment where priorities evolve quickly, proactively bringing structure, clarity, and creative solutions amid uncertainty.

• Highly adaptable. Adjusts quickly to changing business needs, shifting seamlessly between strategic thinking and hands-on execution while maintaining high standards of quality.

• Acts with ownership. Takes initiative, anticipates needs, and follows through with a strong sense of accountability, often operating independently while knowing when to seek input or alignment.

• Collaborates generously. Builds trusted relationships across diverse teams and functions, welcoming feedback, incorporating different perspectives, and contributing to shared success.

• Balances speed with excellence. Delivers high-quality work under tight timelines, exercising sound judgment about when to iterate, when to perfect, and when to move forward.

• Continuously learns and experiments. Embraces new technologies, creative approaches, and ways of working, remaining curious and willing to challenge conventional thinking.

• Communicates with clarity and confidence. Presents ideas clearly, adapts communication for different audiences, and navigates complex conversations with professionalism and good judgment.

• Embraces pioneering thinking. Approaches challenges with curiosity, creativity, and a willingness to question assumptions, helping communicate ideas that don't fit conventional categories while remaining grounded in scientific rigor.

The Digital Sales Executive is responsible for driving the growth of recurring digital revenue across the assigned region through the sale of software, SaaS and cybersecurity solutions. Working in partnership with Key Account Managers, Market Sales teams and the Digital Business Unit, the role identifies, develops and converts opportunities that enhance customer outcomes while accelerating digital transformation and software adoption.

The role acts as the regional digital sales specialist, leading opportunity generation, customer engagement and commercial execution for digital solutions, while contributing to the development of scalable sales methodologies, market strategies and digital growth initiatives.

Duties:

• Own and deliver assigned annual recurring revenue (ARR) and digital sales targets within the designated territory, including achievement of net-new digital/SaaS revenue growth.
