jobs.title: Allround Planner
jobs.description:
Als Allround Planner ben je verantwoordelijk voor het plannen en bewaken van grondstoffen, verpakkingsmaterialen, productie en uitleveringen. Je zorgt ervoor dat materialen op tijd beschikbaar zijn, de productie goed aansluit op de klantvraag en bestellingen volgens afspraak worden geleverd. Daarbij houd je rekening met de productiecapaciteit en voorraadniveaus. Zo zorg je voor een goede planning, betrouwbare leveringen en een efficiënt gebruik van mensen en middelen.

Je komt terecht in een jong, gedreven en ambitieus team waar samenwerken, initiatief nemen en jezelf ontwikkelen centraal staan. Je hebt contact met verschillende collega’s, schakelt snel wanneer de situatie daarom vraagt en denkt mee over oplossingen. Geen dag is hetzelfde en juist die afwisseling maakt het werk uitdagend en leuk. Je krijgt de ruimte om verantwoordelijkheid te nemen, met ideeën te komen en jezelf verder te ontwikkelen. We vinden het belangrijk dat je blijft leren en de kans krijgt om te groeien in je rol.

Wat ga je doen?

In jouw rol ben je verantwoordelijk voor de planning van groene koffie, grondstoffen, verpakkingsmaterialen en productie. Je zorgt ervoor dat materialen op tijd beschikbaar zijn, de productieplanning aansluit op de vraag en voorraden op peil blijven. Daarbij houd je de planning goed in de gaten en stuur je bij wanneer dat nodig is.

Je werkzaamheden bestaan onder andere uit:

• Het opstellen en bijhouden van materiaalbehoeftenplanningen en het plaatsen en opvolgen van bestellingen;
• Het bewaken van leveranciersprestaties, leveringen en de beschikbaarheid en kwaliteit van materialen;
• Het opstellen en aanpassen van productieplanningen, met aandacht voor capaciteit, bezetting en omsteltijden;
• Het afstemmen met de productie over de voortgang en het bijsturen bij veranderingen in de vraag, capaciteit of materiaalbeschikbaarheid;
• Het bewaken van voorraden en het optimaliseren van veiligheidsvoorraden en voorraadparameters.

Naast de dagelijkse planning houd je je bezig met het analyseren van de prestaties van de planning en supply chain. Je stelt rapportages en KPI-overzichten op, signaleert verbeterpunten en ondersteunt verbeterprojecten. Ook help je bij voorraadanalyses en cycle counts en onderneem je actie om overtollige of verouderde voorraden te voorkomen.

Je hebt de bevoegdheid om planningen binnen de afgesproken kaders aan te passen en prioriteiten te stellen voor orders en productieruns. Dreigen er problemen te ontstaan met leveringen, voorraden of capaciteit? Dan signaleer je dit op tijd, schaal je waar nodig op en initieer je corrigerende maatregelen.

Je houdt van plannen, denkt graag vooruit en weet ook bij veranderingen het overzicht te bewaren. Je bent analytisch sterk, werkt nauwkeurig en vindt het leuk om samen met verschillende collega’s tot de beste planning te komen. Je neemt initiatief, durft beslissingen te nemen en blijft ook onder druk resultaatgericht werken.

Daarnaast breng je het volgende mee:

• Je hebt HBO werk- en denkniveau, bij voorkeur met een opleiding in Supply Chain Management, Logistiek, (Technische) Bedrijfskunde of een vergelijkbare richting.
• Je hebt minimaal 2 jaar ervaring met planning binnen een productie-, FMCG- of supplychainomgeving, bijvoorbeeld op het gebied van materiaalplanning, productieplanning of logistieke planning.
• Je hebt ervaring met ERP-systemen. Kennis van SAP, OMP of een vergelijkbaar systeem is een pré.
• Je hebt kennis van Supply Chain Management, MRP-processen, voorraadbeheer en productieplanning en weet je weg te vinden in Excel en planningssystemen.
• Je bent communicatief sterk, organisatorisch vaardig en weet verschillende stakeholders goed mee te nemen.
• Je bent proactief, oplossingsgericht en stressbestendig. Je ziet waar zaken beter kunnen, denkt graag mee over verbeteringen en krijgt energie van een planning die klopt.
• Je beheerst de Nederlandse taal, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk.

De functie valt binnen functiegroep 8 van de Coffee & Tea CAO. Bij JDE krijg je de kans om impact te maken in een dynamische omgeving, samen met collega’s die voor elkaar klaarstaan en successen samen vieren. Je krijgt de ruimte om jezelf te ontwikkelen en bij te dragen aan onze gezamenlijke ambities. Daar hoort natuurlijk ook een goed salaris bij, aangevuld met een uitgebreid pakket aan arbeidsvoorwaarden dat past bij deze functie, waaronder:

• 25 vakantiedagen en 12 ADV dagen;
• 13e maand;
• Persoonlijk opleidingsbudget;
• Korting op de producten van JDE.

DIVERSITY STATEMENT: Samen zijn we JDE!

Voor ons maakt het niet uit wie je bent, waar je vandaan komt, hoe je je leven leidt of hoe je je koffie drinkt. Wij vinden het belangrijk dat JDE een organisatie is waar iedereen kan bijdragen, groeien en ontwikkelen. Elk land, iedere cultuur en elk individu heeft een uniek verhaal waar we naar luisteren. Door met diverse collega’s samen te werken binnen een inclusieve cultuur lukt het ons iedereen welkom te heten in de wereld van koffie en thee

Enthousiast? Solliciteer direct!

Ben je geïnteresseerd in deze vacature, dan kun je reageren ter attentie van Patrick Braak (Planning & Logistics Manager) en Iris Minnesma (Talent Acquisition Specialist).

JDE Peet’s - now part of Keurig Dr Pepper – is the world’s leading pure-play coffee company, with a presence in more than 100 markets. Guided by our ‘Reignite the Amazing’ strategy, we are focused on brand-led growth across three big bets: Peet’s, L’OR, and our 10 strategically selected local icons led by Jacobs.

jobs.title: Social Media Manager
jobs.description:
About AppLovin

AppLovin makes technologies that help businesses of every size connect to their ideal customers. The company provides end-to-end advertising solutions for businesses to reach, monetize and grow their global audiences. For more information about AppLovin, visit: www.applovin.com.

To deliver on this mission, our global team is composed of team members with life experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives that mirror our developers and customers around the world. At AppLovin, we are intentional about the team and culture we are building, seeking candidates who are outstanding in their own right and also demonstrate their support of others.

About Gist
Gist is a new consumer social app built by AppLovin, a handbook for the curious. We’re building our brand and community from the ground up, and we’re looking for a Social Media Manager who is as comfortable creating content as they are reading the data behind it.
In this role, you’ll own Gist’s voice and presence across social. You’ll create, test, and iterate on content that is genuinely useful and worth sharing, and you’ll stay close to the metrics that tell you what’s working.

About the Role
We are launching a new social platform dedicated to the relatable, actionable content that people use to navigate their daily lives.
We are looking for a Social Media Manager to be the face and voice of Gist across the platforms where our audience already lives: Instagram, TikTok, Threads, Substack, and whatever comes next.
This is a builder role. We want someone who has grown an audience from zero, knows what makes content travel on each platform, and move faster than anyone around them.
You will own our social channels end to end and be the reason people discover Gist before they ever download it.

A Day in the Life

• Own social strategy and execution across Instagram, TikTok, Threads, Substack, and emerging platforms.
• Create platform-native content, including short-form video, posts, and written pieces, in a distinct Gist voice.
• Work with agencies, individual content creators, and influencers, including our own Gist creators, to produce posts and feature them in our content.
• Grow our audience and engagement through fast experimentation: test formats and hooks, study what lands, and double down.
• Partner with performance marketing so social supports the broader growth funnel.
• Track and report on audience growth, engagement, and content performance to shape what we make next.
• Spot trends and cultural moments early, and know which ones are worth jumping on.

The Impact You’ll Make

• Define how Gist looks, sounds, and feels in public from launch.
• Build an owned audience across platforms that becomes a durable growth channel for the product.
• Establish repeatable content playbooks and formats that scale as the team and the platform grow.
• Bring ground-level insight on what resonates with our audience directly into product and brand decisions.

Who You Are

• 2-3+ years of experience in social media, content, or community growth.
• A proven history of growing an account or channel from the ground up to a significant, engaged audience. You can show us the results and walk us through how you did it.
• Fluent with AI tools, with a clear point of view on how to use them to create better content faster.
• Strong writing, visual, and editing instincts, with a portfolio of content you made yourself.
• Comfortable creating across formats and platforms, from Instagram and TikTok video to Threads and Substack writing.
• Self-directed and fast-moving, and at home in an ambiguous, early-stage environment.
• Experience working with or inside a larger organization while owning your channels with startup-level autonomy.

Nice to Have

• Experience as a UGC creator or content creator yourself.
• Experience as a brand marketer at other startups.
• Experience writing, growing, or running a Substack.
• Familiarity with lifestyle feed content dynamics: what drives daily engagement, retention, and shareability.

Why Join This Venture

• This is more than a social role. It’s a chance to build the public identity of a new consumer product inside an industry leader.
• Enjoy the autonomy of a startup, backed by AppLovin’s resources, technology, and scale.
• Work with a lean, fast-moving team that values creativity, speed, and good taste.
• High visibility into how brand and content drive product growth, with a direct line to leadership from day one.

AppLovin is proud to be an equal opportunity employer that is committed to inclusion and diversity. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status, or other legally protected characteristics. Learn more about EEO rights as an applicant here.

If you need assistance and/or a reasonable accommodation due to a disability during the application or recruiting process, please send us a request at jobs@applovin.com

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.description:
About AppLovin

AppLovin makes technologies that help businesses of every size connect to their ideal customers. The company provides end-to-end advertising solutions for businesses to reach, monetize and grow their global audiences. For more information about AppLovin, visit: www.applovin.com.

To deliver on this mission, our global team is composed of team members with life experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives that mirror our developers and customers around the world. At AppLovin, we are intentional about the team and culture we are building, seeking candidates who are outstanding in their own right and also demonstrate their support of others.

About the Role
We’re building a next-generation global content platform that helps people turn real-life experiences into valuable stories for others. We’re a small, high-caliber founding team, backed by AppLovin’s technology, data capabilities, and global reach.
We’re looking for a Product Manager in Palo Alto to be the voice of the user. You’ll own how we learn about our users and the US market, then turn what you learn into product decisions. Most of your time will go to talking with users, studying the market, and digging through feedback, and you’ll translate all of it into clear insights that shape our roadmap.

A Day in the Life

• Independently plan and run user research: recruit participants, conduct interviews, and synthesize findings
• Run market and competitive research on our features and product, including spending real time in other apps to understand what works and why
• Turn feedback from support tickets, Apple App Store and Google Play reviews, and community channels into structured product insights
• Dig into why users return, stay active, or drop off, and recommend specific actions to improve retention and engagement
• Identify what motivates the users to share, engage, and come back, and propose distinctive, culturally resonant features
• Partner closely with Engineering and Operations to turn insights into roadmap priorities
• Present findings and recommendations clearly to the team and leadership

The Impact You’ll Make

• Be the user voice: Bring a real understanding of culture and behavior into every product decision.
• Turn feedback into direction: Build a repeatable system that converts raw feedback into prioritized insights.
• Shape what we build: Your research will directly influence which features we build, change, or cut.
• Drive retention and engagement: Combine qualitative insight with usage data to improve returning and active users.

Who You Are

• 3-6 years of experience in product management, product marketing, strategy and operations, consulting, user research, or a similar analytical role.
• A startup background and mindset: you’ve worked in early-stage or fast-growing teams, taken on a much bigger scope than your title suggested, and moved things forward without waiting to be told what to do
• Strong initiative and ownership: you spot problems and opportunities on your own and drive them to a result
• Strong sense for the culture, trends, and how people use social and content apps
• Warm and approachable, with the ability to put people at ease and draw out honest, thoughtful answers in interviews
• Strong product sense: you’re curious about apps, have opinions about what makes them good or bad, and enjoy picking products apart
• A structured thinker who can synthesize messy qualitative input into clear, actionable conclusions
• Comfortable with data, and able to pair qualitative findings with usage metrics
• Comfortable with ambiguity and a fast-moving environment

Nice to Have

• Experience in consumer, social, community, or content products
• A background in consulting, market research, or user research
• Experience analyzing app store reviews or support data at scale
• Interest in a long-term career in product management

Why Join

• Join at the founding stage of a global consumer product, with direct visibility and impact
• Take on a broad scope early, with the autonomy to own problems end to end and see your work shape the product
• Work in a small, collaborative team where ideas are debated openly and ownership is real
• Get the backing of AppLovin’s scale, technology, and resources

jobs.description:
Ebury helps ambitious businesses unlock global growth, and we take the same approach with our people. We encourage innovation and movement, collaboration and problem-solving, and foster an environment where everyone can feel they belong, are valued, supported and empowered to succeed.

If you’re a collaborator who wants to help transform how businesses operate globally, get in touch - we’d love to discuss how Ebury can accelerate your career so you can shape the future.

Associate Legal Counsel - Finance or Derivatives Lawyer

Ebury London Leon Office - Hybrid: 4 days in the office, 1 day working from home per week

The Legal Department at Ebury is core to the functioning of the Ebury Group.  It provides front-line advice to all parts of the Ebury Group on legal, regulatory and governance matters which contribute to Ebury’s growth every day.

We are looking for an enthusiastic and driven finance and / or derivatives lawyer who is keen to work in a fast-paced, dynamic and growing company. The successful candidate will provide high quality legal advice to key stakeholders globally and be pivotal to Ebury’s development on a global scale.  While advising on financial matters is key, this role will also enable the person who fills it to turn their hand to commercial matters and a variety of other matters with a view to supporting the development of the person that fills this role.  The person who fills this role will report to a Senior Legal Counsel.

Key responsibilities include:

• drafting and advising on relationship agreements and other terms with customers, including ISDAs, FX T&Cs, supplier payment finance T&Cs, in particular for our institutional customer base.

• contributing to the design and implementation of new products (including cryptocurrency and foreign exchange derivatives) and expansion into new markets;

• preparing customer documentation in relation to complex structures such as funds and SPVs;

• working with Front Office, Treasury, Risk, HR, Operations and other departments to resolve day-to-day queries;

• structuring and executing strategic initiatives such as refinancings and negotiations with banking partners;

• representing Ebury in interaction with clients, counterparties, banking partners, industry bodies and other third parties;

• preparing templates, playbooks, procedures and self-service material and participating in the provision of relevant training and awareness programmes; and

• advising on corporate structuring matters, working closely with the Chief Financial Officer and Chief Legal Officer to maintain and develop Ebury’s corporate structure given its global footprint in an efficient manner, having regarding to regulatory, tax and other relevant matters;

• drafting and negotiating agreements required to support Ebury’s business and operational activity with third parties and on an intragroup basis. and

• helping the legal team improve their processes using AI, including proposing and carrying out initiatives using the AI tools the team works with.

Key skills requirements include:

• a proactive mindset and an ability to communicate effectively in practical terms with stakeholders at all levels of the Ebury Group;

• a legal qualification in a jurisdiction where Ebury has a significant presence;

• at least 3 years of legal experience, either in private practice or in house in either banking and finance or derivatives;

• interest in the fintech sector and financial products;

• fluent in English (C1, advanced level); and

• an ability in a fast paced environment to prioritise and manage a wide range of competing priorities (with support from other team members and external counsel where necessary).

Why Ebury?

• Competitive Starting Salary with an annual discretionary bonus that truly rewards your performance from day one.

• Dedicated Mentorship: Learn directly from experienced managers who are invested in your success.

• Cutting-Edge Technology: Leverage state-of-the-art tailor made tools and systems that enable you to perform at your best.

• Clear, Accelerated Career Progression: Defined pathways to leadership and specialist roles within Ebury.

• Dynamic & Supportive Culture: Work in a collaborative environment where teamwork and personal growth are prioritised.

• Generous Benefits Package: Access competitive benefits tailored to your location, which typically include health care and social benefits.

• Central Office: A fantastic location with excellent transport links.

Ready to launch your career with a global FinTech? Click the ‘Apply’ Today and discover your potential at Ebury!

About us

Ebury delivers sophisticated, integrated solutions — business accounts, hedging, and financing — on a single platform with a seamless workflow. Our success is built on a simple premise and singular purpose: To help businesses operate and scale globally.

Since its founding in 2009, Ebury has always been a fast-growing leader in fintech. Today, we bring together 2000+ Eburians across nearly 70 cities and we’re always looking to add to our team.

At the heart of our offering is a proprietary platform, purpose-built to help businesses seamlessly streamline and manage global cash flow. We focus on continuous product evolution and innovation to build the infrastructure for borderless growth and help our clients scale at every stage.

The opportunities at Ebury are as diverse as our people, ranging from business development to engineering roles across our tech pillars.

We believe in inclusion. We stand against discrimination in all forms and are against the intolerance of differences that makes us a modern and successful organisation. At Ebury, you can be whoever you want to be and still feel a sense of belonging no matter your story.

jobs.title: Comms Lead
jobs.description:
Slingshot AI

Slingshot AI is the team behind Ash, the first AI designed for mental health. Our mission is to make support more accessible and help people change their lives in the ways they want.

We’re building a world-class team by empowering individuals with the autonomy, flexibility, and support they need to do their best work. We dream big, iterate fast, and care deeply. If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you.

Our team spans machine learning, product, engineering, conversational design, clinical, growth, and operations, with offices in both New York City and London.

We're a well-funded Series A company, having raised $93M from Andreessen Horowitz, Radical Ventures, Forerunner Ventures, plus top-tier tech investors involved in ElevenLabs, Captions, Shopify, Plaid, Notion, Canva, Twitch, Airtable, and many others.




THE ROLE

Millions of people already use AI for their mental health. Most of them use a general chatbot that was never built for it. We designed Ash for this, and we do the research on who it helps and why. Nobody else can tell that story. The people who decide what the public believes about AI therapy (reporters, lawmakers, payers, therapists, investors) mostly hear the fear scenarios, and they hear them from people who are not building the product or doing the research.

You will be our first in-house Comms Lead and the editor-in-chief of everything Slingshot says publicly. You tell the stories of our research, our safety work, our clinicians, and our users, and you turn them into pieces people read and share. This could take the form of written pieces, 90 second videos, headlines, LinkedIn posts, panel talks, pitches to reporters, and more.

We have an unusual amount of raw material: clinical trials with long follow up, research across hundreds of thousands of users, safety audits at a scale that is rare in this category, published papers, academic partners, a safety system and benchmarks we have never properly shown, and a growing number of users who want to tell their story. What we lack is the person with the taste to spot the story inside a research finding and the speed to ship it the same week.

You will own the publishing cadence and write most of the pieces yourself. Where it helps, you bring in outside help for pitching and placement, and you decide which pieces go out and in what order. You do not need to edit video, but you need to be able to brief a producer so the result is good.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Stay on top of early areas of interest internally and externally. Stay aware of internal teams developing a benchmark, model, study, safety feature, and more as well as what cultural conversations are taking place to curate a running list of what stories are worth telling externally.

 - Build compelling stories. Pull out something that is new or surprising from our research, user stories, safety work, and more. Figure out how it connects with the audience we care about and the conversations they are already hearing. Write a headline a normal person would click, without dumbing it down.

 - Publish consistently and quickly in relevant channels, including working with reporters. Blog posts, research write-ups, LinkedIn posts, short videos, press releases, etc. should be going out weekly. You are the best placed person to own relationships with reporters that we already have and make them useful for us. We work on a lot and work fast, so there’s always something interesting to say!

 - Make our approach, people, and evidence visible. The stories we put out should include material about our safety approach, clinical frameworks, trial results that currently exist only internally. Also, our team is amazing and you can support our founders, researchers, and clinicians posting and speaking in their own areas.

 - Own our core messages and the safety conversation. Figure out the most compelling core messages we want to tell and communicate them across surfaces, channels, and formats. Safety is the first thing many people we talk to in the field ask about and we have more evidence on it than anyone else. You own turning the evidence we have into answers we are ready to give when asked.


ABOUT YOU

 - You balance taste with urgency. You know what makes a story compelling vs. marketing slop, but understand that comms needs to contribute to business goals (signups, B2B leads, or fundraising buzz).

 - You can turn deep technical information into accessible stories. You can quickly understand how a complex safety system or intricate clinical study works and translate that into a story that is easy to understand. You can take a complex methods section from an academic paper and turn it into a sentence that would answer the key question a general reader would have.

 - You use all the tools you need to tell a story, but are writing-forward. You can write a technical blog post in your sleep, but can also write a script for a video producer to create a clip that would accompany your article. You also can bring in freelancers, editors, or agencies to build on the work you do and manage them where appropriate.

jobs.title: Executive Administrative Assistant
jobs.description:
Global Partnerships & Channels (GPC)

At ServiceNow, we put AI to work for people. Our AI platform connects any AI, any data, and any workflow to help organizations work smarter, move faster, and reinvent how business gets done. Global Partnerships & Channels extends that impact through a worldwide ecosystem of strategic, technology, cloud, service, and solution partners.

Role Overview

The Executive Administrative Assistant (EAA) to the GPC Leader is a highly trusted administrative partner responsible for maximizing the effectiveness, productivity, and operating capacity of a global executive leading one of ServiceNow’s most strategic and fast-moving organizations.

This is an AI-forward executive support role requiring demonstrated proficiency with AI-enabled Executive Assistant (AI EA) tools and platforms, in addition to broader AI and automation capabilities. The successful candidate already uses AI EA tools as an integrated part of how they manage executive calendars, scheduling, meeting preparation, follow-up, travel, communications, task management, and executive-office workflows.

We are looking for someone who can show how they have personally used AI EA technology to improve the way an executive office operates—not simply someone who is familiar with AI, uses a general-purpose AI assistant, or is interested in learning these tools.

The GPC Leader operates at an exceptionally fast pace across a global ecosystem of ServiceNow executives, customers, partners, industry leaders, and employees. Priorities can shift rapidly and often require immediate action. The EAA must operate with exceptional agility, adaptability, flexibility, judgment, and precision while maintaining accuracy and continuity across a constantly changing executive agenda.

This role goes well beyond traditional calendar administration. The EAA is a force multiplier for the executive, combining exceptional executive support capabilities with AI EA technology, automation, and modern productivity practices to anticipate needs, eliminate friction, create operating leverage, and continually improve how work gets done.

What You’ll Do

AI EA Tools, Automation & Executive Productivity

• Demonstrate advanced, hands-on proficiency using AI-enabled Executive Assistant tools and platforms specifically designed to support executive administration and executive-office workflows.

• Integrate AI EA tools into daily work to improve complex scheduling, calendar optimization, meeting preparation, briefing and context development, action and commitment tracking, follow-up, travel coordination, communications, and executive workflow management.

• Use AI EA capabilities to anticipate conflicts, identify scheduling and workflow dependencies, surface outstanding actions, organize executive priorities, and reduce administrative friction.

• Determine which work is best performed through specialized AI EA tools, broader AI platforms, workflow automation, or direct human judgment and intervention.

• Build and continually improve an AI-enabled administrative operating model that increases executive capacity while maintaining exceptional accuracy, discretion, responsiveness, and stakeholder experience.

• Identify repetitive or inefficient administrative processes and redesign them using AI EA capabilities, automation, integrations, templates, and other productivity technologies.

• Apply appropriate quality controls to AI-supported work, independently validating outputs and maintaining accountability for accuracy, confidentiality, and final execution.

• Remain current on emerging AI EA technologies and proactively evaluate and adopt capabilities that can measurably improve executive and administrative productivity.

Executive Calendar, Time & Priority Management

• Own a highly complex, dynamic global executive calendar involving C-suite leaders, senior internal executives, customers, strategic partners, industry leaders, and employees.

• Manage the calendar as a strategic business tool, ensuring executive time is aligned to the highest-value business, customer, partner, talent, and leadership priorities.

• Make rapid, thoughtful decisions when priorities change, understanding what can move, what cannot, who needs to be informed, and what downstream implications must be addressed.

• Anticipate conflicts, preparation requirements, decision points, travel implications, and follow-up needs before they become issues.

• Reprioritize quickly and confidently in an environment where the executive’s schedule may change multiple times in a day.

• Protect focus time while preserving the flexibility required of a highly visible global leader.

Internal & External Executive Engagements

• Orchestrate internal and external executive engagements from initial request through preparation, execution, and follow-up.

• Coordinate engagements with ServiceNow executives, customers, partners, industry leaders, external organizations, and other high-priority stakeholders.

• Ensure the executive enters critical engagements with the right context, objectives, participants, materials, logistics, and preparation.

• Maintain visibility to commitments and follow-up resulting from executive engagements and ensure actions move forward quickly.

• Coordinate across executive offices and external organizations to create a highly professional, responsive, and seamless stakeholder experience.

• Represent the GPC Leader with discretion, confidence, sound judgment, and strong executive presence.

GPC Leadership & Operating Rhythm

• Enable the operating rhythm of the GPC leadership team, including leadership meetings, business reviews, planning sessions, executive offsites, talent discussions, company events, and key partner engagements.

• Partner closely with the Chief of Staff to translate business priorities into an effective executive cadence and use of the leader’s time.

• Maintain a working understanding of GPC priorities, key decisions, leadership commitments, and upcoming milestones so administrative decisions can be made with appropriate business context.

• Connect meetings, decisions, commitments, and follow-up rather than treating individual calendar events as isolated activities.

• Anticipate what the leader and leadership team will need next and initiate action without waiting for direction.

Cross-Functional Executive Office Partnership

• Work closely with the Chief of Staff, HR Business Partner, Executive Communications, Finance, Strategy, and other key functions to coordinate and sequence executive priorities.

• Serve as a highly effective connector across teams, ensuring information, decisions, requests, and follow-up move at the pace required by the business.

• Coordinate executive communications, leadership forums, company events, talent engagements, organizational activities, and external commitments.

• Establish strong working relationships with executive assistants across ServiceNow and with the offices of customers, partners, and other external executives.

Global Travel & Executive Logistics

• Manage complex domestic and international travel, including rapidly changing itineraries, executive meetings, partner/customer engagements, events, and associated logistics.

• Anticipate travel dependencies and resolve issues quickly, often with limited notice and across multiple time zones.

• Integrate travel, meetings, preparation, and executive priorities into a cohesive plan rather than managing each independently.

• Remain highly responsive when critical executive needs or schedule changes require flexibility outside traditional working hours.

What You Bring

• Certification in Certified Administrative Professional (CAP) or equivalent administrative credential preferred.

• 7+ years of progressive experience supporting senior executives, preferably at the SVP, EVP, or C-suite level in a global technology, high-growth, or similarly fast-paced environment.

• Demonstrated proficiency with AI-enabled Executive Assistant (AI EA) tools and platforms. This is a core requirement of the role—not simply general familiarity or fluency with AI.

• Proven experience personally incorporating AI EA tools into executive administrative workflows such as complex calendar and scheduling management, meeting preparation, executive briefing, action tracking, follow-up, travel, communications, and productivity management.

• Ability to provide specific examples of AI EA tools used, the executive-administration problems addressed, how the tools were incorporated into daily workflows, and the resulting improvements in speed, efficiency, accuracy, or executive capacity.

• Broader proficiency with generative AI, workflow automation, and productivity technologies, with the ability to combine these capabilities with specialized AI EA tools.

• Demonstrated success supporting a global executive operating at exceptional speed, with complex stakeholder demands and priorities that can change rapidly.

• Exceptional agility, adaptability, and flexibility, including the ability to reprioritize and execute quickly without sacrificing accuracy.

• Exceptional attention to detail and a demonstrated record of accuracy in high-volume, high-velocity executive environments.

• Advanced ability to manage highly complex global calendars and make independent prioritization decisions with limited direction.

• A productivity and continuous-improvement mindset: instinctively identifies opportunities to simplify, automate, standardize, eliminate unnecessary work, and improve how the executive office operates.

• Exceptional judgment, discretion, executive presence, and ability to manage highly sensitive and confidential information.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills and confidence engaging with senior internal executives, customers, partners, and external stakeholders.

• A highly anticipatory working style—the ability to recognize what is needed, understand implications, and act before being asked.

• Ability to remain composed and highly effective amid ambiguity, urgency, last-minute change, and competing demands.

What Success Looks Like

• The GPC Leader has more capacity because of this partnership. Executive time is focused on the highest-value priorities, administrative friction is reduced, and the executive office operates at extraordinary speed without sacrificing accuracy or stakeholder experience.

• AI EA technology is embedded in the day-to-day operation of the executive office. Specialized AI EA tools, broader AI capabilities, and automation are intentionally applied to reduce administrative burden, accelerate execution, improve accuracy, strengthen follow-through, and increase executive capacity.

• Internal and external executive engagements are exceptionally well orchestrated. The leader has the right context at the right time; stakeholders receive timely, professional engagement; commitments do not get lost; and changes are absorbed without unnecessary disruption.

• The EAA is a trusted extension of the GPC Leader—able to keep pace, anticipate what is coming, adapt immediately when circumstances change, and continually increase the productivity of the executive and broader leadership team.

Why This Role Matters

Global Partnerships & Channels is central to how ServiceNow expands customer value, scales innovation, and brings the power of the ServiceNow AI platform to market through a global partner ecosystem. The Executive Administrative Assistant is a critical enabler of that mission—creating focus, connectivity, productivity, and operating leverage for the GPC Leader and leadership team.

Work Personas

We approach our distributed world of work with flexibility and trust. Work personas (flexible, remote, or required in office) are categories that are assigned to ServiceNow employees depending on the nature of their work and their assigned work location. Learn more here. To determine eligibility for a work persona, ServiceNow may confirm the distance between your primary residence and the closest ServiceNow office using a third-party service.

Equal Opportunity Employer

ServiceNow is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, gender identity,  veteran status, or any other category protected by law. In addition, all qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with legal requirements.

Accommodations

We strive to create an accessible and inclusive experience for all candidates. If you require a reasonable accommodation to complete any part of the application process, or are unable to use this online application and need an alternative method to apply, please contact globaltalentss@servicenow.com for assistance.

Export Control Regulations

For positions requiring access to controlled technology subject to export control regulations, including the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR), ServiceNow may be required to obtain export control approval from government authorities for certain individuals. All employment is contingent upon ServiceNow obtaining any export license or other approval that may be required by relevant export control authorities.

jobs.title: Operations Manager - Dallas
jobs.description:
Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.



THE TEAM
• ~160 people,  around half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

The Opportunity

This is not a legacy logistics job. This is a chance to launch Relay into the Americas.

You will report to the Site Manager/Head of Site and will run shifts at one of our Hybrid Sort Centres (HSCs), leading 50–100+ operatives through high-volume, time-pressured sortation where minutes matter and small deviations cascade into missed deadlines.

You will also be accountable for whether the site is measurably better in a month than it is today for each of our key metrics. You are on the floor for your shift, every shift. This is not a project role with occasional site visits and it is not a desk job, the forward work happens alongside running the operation.



Who will thrive in this role

 - Deliver shift plan end to end people deployment, throughput, quality standards, and health & safety compliance

 - Lead, develop, and performance-manage a frontline team of 50–100+ operatives

 - Build the mechanisms that hold the operation together. Build controls, cadences, metrics, SOPs, change management and own their adoption, not only their design

 - Plan ahead for future shifts; labour, training, and the risks you can see coming before they land

 - Own the end-of-shift handover; what happened, what is at risk, what the next shift needs to know

 - Stay decisive through volume peaks, outages, and labour gaps. Triage, solve the problem at hand quickly, contain the impact, restore flow

 - Present and write clearly whether briefs, escalations, handovers or post-incident reviews. Decisions here get made based off what you wrote

 - Implement changes into a live operation such as introducing robotics, launching new sortation tech or onboarding new clients. We are changing the operations constantly which means you’ll roll change out mid flight and bring your team along the journey.



Who you are

 - Scaled something from zero: a site, a market, a process or a program.

 - Managed a physical operation: quick commerce, grocery, e-commerce fulfillment, last mile, 3PL, food production, airport ground handling, rail. Anywhere with a hard cut off and people on the floor.

 - Communicate in both directions and have strong people management skills: you can brief 80 operatives at shift start and take a problem to senior leadership the same day.

 - Built a mechanism that held: a control, a cadence, a metric, a document standard. Something you authored that changed how frontline teams worked.

 - Own numbers rather than report them: you can name a metric you created or redefined, explain why the previous one was wrong, and say what changed afterwards.

 - Understand frontline work: one of these must be true: you have personally led frontline teams; you have worked embedded in and around a frontline population day to day, without the reporting line; or you have been accountable for outcomes delivered by frontline people you did not employ.

You do not need to have worked in parcels, fulfilment, or sortation. Several of our most talented people had not.



Backgrounds that translate well

 - Program Manager in a logistics or e-commerce business

 - Operations Excellence and Continuous Improvement

 - Strategy & Operations

 - Transformation manager

 - Launch and Expansion Manager

 - Regional operations manager
   
   

We have hired well from corporate operations, from central operations inside large UK retailers and carriers, and from quick commerce and marketplace operators. Consulting backgrounds work where you implemented, not only recommended; we are keen to understand what you who actually rolled it out.

Who Thrives at Relay?

 - Aim with Precision: You define problems clearly and measure your impact meticulously.

 - Play to Win: You chase bold bets, tackle the hard stuff, and view constraints as fuel, not friction.

 - 1% Better Every Day: You believe that small, consistent improvements lead to exponential growth. You move quickly, deliver results, and learn from every experience.

 - All In, All the Time: You show up and step up. You take ownership from start to finish and do what it takes to deliver when it counts.

 - People-Powered Greatness: You invest in your teammates. You give and receive feedback with care and candour. You build trust through high standards and shared success.

 - Grow the Whole Pie: You seek out win-win solutions for merchants, couriers, and our customers, because when they thrive, so do we.
   
   If these resonate, and you combine strong technical fundamentals with entrepreneurial drive, let’s connect.



Relay is an equal-opportunity employer committed to diversity, inclusion, and fostering a workplace where everyone thrives.

jobs.title: Platform Deployment Engineer - West Coast
jobs.description:
Neural Concept embeds AI into design and simulation workflows so engineering teams make continuous, data-driven decisions instead of waiting on sequential design–simulation–validation cycles. None of that matters until the platform is running inside the customer's environment, on their infrastructure, under their rules.


That is this role. You take an enterprise customer and make the platform real for them: architected, deployed, integrated, cleared by their security organisation, and stable enough that their engineers stop thinking about it. You own that outcome end to end for named accounts, as their primary technical counterpart.



What you will do 

 - The deployment, from the first architecture conversation through go-live and into steady-state operation.

 - Its integration with the customer's identity, data and engineering systems, and the infrastructure and model serving layer beneath it.

 - The relationship with their IT, security and platform teams: assessments, architecture reviews, and the call when something breaks.

 - The diagnosis when it does break, including when the cause sits outside our own software.

 - The runbooks, post-mortems and playbooks that make the next deployment easier, and the feedback loop into Product.



Where you will do it
Managed Kubernetes across the major clouds. On-premises and fully air-gapped clusters with no route to the internet, GPU infrastructure, self-hosted model serving. Customer HPC environments, schedulers, and shared storage under real load.



If installing software with no internet access, on hardware you do not control, reads as the interesting part of the job rather than the obstacle, this will suit you.



Who you are 

You will often be the only Neural Concept engineer in the room. We are looking for someone with:

 - 6+ years deploying and operating enterprise software in production, two of them in environments you did not control.

 - Kubernetes at configuration depth: how chart values become rendered manifests, and why a workload will not start.

 - Identity and SSO fundamentals: OIDC and SAML, clients and credential rotation, redirect URIs, group-to-role mapping.

 - Linux, networking and TLS: DNS, routing, ingress and egress, certificate chains and interception proxies.

 - Kubernetes storage: persistent volumes and CSI, access modes, diagnosing shared storage that degrades under load.

 - A production deployment you personally carried and then supported. Name it, date it, tell us what went wrong.

 - Professional customer-facing English, and willingness to travel and work your customers' hours.

Also valuable: regulated or air-gapped deployments · private registries and image mirroring · GPU scheduling and LLM serving · enterprise IdP administration · Terraform and GitOps · Prometheus and Grafana · HPC schedulers · ISO 27001 evidence · Python · PLM, CAD or CAE exposure.



You Get

 - Work with a world-class technology team – our engineers are top-notch, and we always aim for excellence.

 - Benefit from a competitive salary and rewarding opportunities as we continue to scale.

 - Thrive in a collaborative, multicultural environment where your work is visible and recognized.

 - Develop professionally alongside talented colleagues who share knowledge freely and support one another.

 - Make a global impact by helping customers shift to AI-assisted design, making innovation faster, smarter, and more sustainable.

 - Balance life and work with remote work or hybrid model (20% remote) —we care about results, not rigid schedules.

 - Enjoy paid vacations, healthcare (medical/vision/dental), 401K matching



Where You Will Be

 - San Mateo, California; 

 - Travelling: This position will require travelling to customer locations in the US.

 - Start date: ASAP

 - Eligibility: ITAR clearance required 


WE'RE PROUD TO BE AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER, AND WE'RE COMMITTED TO BUILDING A DIVERSE AND INCLUSIVE ENVIRONMENT WHERE YOU CAN THRIVE.

jobs.title: Trustee
jobs.description:
IFRS Foundation calls for nominations for a Trustee from Europe for 2027

The IFRS Foundation is an independent, not-for-profit organisation created in 2001 to develop—in the public interest—high-quality, understandable, enforceable and globally accepted standards for financial reporting, and to promote and facilitate their adoption. This is done through its two standard-setting boards: the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB), which sets IFRS® Accounting Standards, and the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB), which sets IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards.

The Trustees of the IFRS Foundation oversee the Foundation and are accountable to a Monitoring Board of public authorities.

The 22 Trustees are appointed from Africa, the Americas, Asia–Oceania, Europe and ‘at large’ (any area of the world), and come from varied professional backgrounds. They are responsible for governance and organisational strategy; for maintaining the Foundation’s Constitution and the Due Process Handbook; for appointing members to the IASB, the ISSB, the IFRS Interpretations Committee and various advisory bodies; and for funding. Trustees also assume the role of company directors in accordance with the UK Overseas Companies Regulations 2009.

The Foundation is seeking a new Trustee from Europe to fill a vacancy that will arise on 1 January 2027.

Qualified candidates will have senior-level experience from any broad array of professional backgrounds and an interest in corporate reporting. They will be able to demonstrate a firm commitment to serving the public interest, to the work of the Foundation and to the IASB and the ISSB as high-quality global standard-setters and will be knowledgeable about finance. They must be able to meet the time commitment, which includes, but is not limited to, at least three three-day meetings each year held in different locations around the world and serve on Trustee committees that meet during the three-day meetings as well as on an ad hoc basis via video calls.

Trustees are expected to engage with stakeholders in the markets in their geographical region. Trustees should understand, and be sensitive to, the challenges associated with the adoption and application of high-quality global accounting and sustainability disclosure standards. They should also have knowledge of relevant current issues, such as the effect of new technologies on corporate reporting and developments in investor and market information needs.

Current employees of organisations represented on the Monitoring Board are not eligible for consideration.

The appointment is for three years. The term may be renewed for another three years.

Read about the role of Trustees and how the Foundation ensures the group of Trustees remains diverse with an appropriate balance of professional backgrounds.

Please apply through our job board. Include a covering letter and CV addressed to Ken Robinson, Chair of the IFRS Foundation Nominating Committee. Applications are due by 30 November 2026.

***The Trustees have the discretion to review applications received after the specified date***

Read about our  appointment process and the Trustee role specification to learn more about this opportunity and the Foundation at ifrs.org.

About us

At the IFRS Foundation, we believe better information leads to better decisions. We set financial reporting standards that enable companies to meet the evolving information needs of the global capital markets. United by our purpose to foster trust, growth and long-term financial stability in the global economy, we engage in challenging, meaningful work every day—across all our areas of expertise.

If you share our passion for this mission, we want to hear from you.

Diverse perspectives. International expertise.

Working for our global organisation offers many benefits, including:

• rewarding work that serves the public interest;

• engagement with diverse international experts;

• inclusive and collaborative teams;

• intellectually challenging projects;

• flexible working arrangements;

• numerous areas of specialisation; and

• opportunities for professional growth and development.

Diversity and inclusion are seen as key strengths of our organisation. These qualities are essential for us to engage with and meet the needs of our varied global stakeholders, and they are part of what makes the IFRS Foundation a great place to work.
