jobs.title: Registered Dietitian
jobs.description:
Weekly outpatient therapy isn't always enough, and a trip to the ER isn't the only answer. Patients and their families rely on Compass Health Center when in crisis – every day, we help people overcome depression, anxiety, suicidality, obsessions/compulsions, trauma, chronic pain, and other obstacles in order for our patients to live freely.

About This Role

As a Registered Dietitian in the Eating Disorders Program, you’ll provide nutrition therapy and support to patients whose relationship with food is the primary target of treatment. You’ll meet with patients individually, facilitate clinical nutrition groups, and provide direct support during meals and snacks. You’ll partner closely with Primary Therapists, Group Therapists, Family Therapists, and Psychiatry Team Members to ensure comprehensive and compassionate care. Reports to the Associate Director of the Eating Disorders Program, with a dotted line clinically to the Director of the Eating Disorders Program, who oversees all clinical aspects of the program.

This role is an onsite role at our Northbrook location working within our Adult (ages 18+) Eating Disorders Program. At times, this role will include virtually supporting our other locations, as well as our Adolescent Programming as indicated.

What You'll Do:

Nutrition Assessment and Care Planning

• Complete nutrition assessments at admission, including all aspects of nutrition care process—diagnosis, intervention, monitoring, and evaluation planning

• Develop individualized meal plans that support nutritional rehabilitation and progressive exposure to avoided and feared foods

• Establish and revise individually determined, biologically appropriate weight ranges in collaboration with the treatment team

• Collaborate with nursing and prescribers to assess and monitor ongoing medical status, including weights, vital signs, and lab values, and adjust nutrition interventions accordingly

• Revise the nutrition plan as intake, medical status, and treatment targets change

Individual Nutrition Sessions

• Meet with patients individually to review intake, adjust the meal plan, and set nutrition-related treatment targets

• Address food rules, ritualized eating, compensatory behaviors, and avoidance directly

• Support provision of nutrition interventions, including structured food exposure planning

• Address exercise, movement, and compensatory activity in collaboration with the treatment team

• Prepare patients for independent eating at step-down and discharge, including grocery preparation and restaurant planning

Group Facilitation and Eating Support

• Facilitate clinical nutrition groups within the program curriculum

• Facilitate applied nutrition groups, including in vivo food-based interventions

• Provide required coverage during supported meals and snacks

• Coach patients through meal completion, distress, and post-meal urges

• Communicate intake and behavioral observations to the treatment team

Care Coordination

• Partner with the other members of the treatment team to align nutrition targets with the case formulation and treatment targets

• Contribute nutrition and medical observations during interdisciplinary rounds

• Serve as the program’s resource on nutrition status and needs for prescribers, nursing, and clinical staff

• Provide nutrition education to families and support people in partnership with the Family Therapist

• Coordinate with outpatient dietitians and medical providers through nutrition aftercare handoff

• Contribute nutrition documentation supporting initial and continued insurance authorization

Program Operations

• Participate in required program training, fidelity monitoring, supervision, and consultation

• Complete required documentation throughout treatment

• Contribute to development of program nutrition standards, meal structure, curriculum development and revision, and food sourcing practices

• Other duties, as assigned

Who You Are:

Credentials and Experience

• Master’s degree in dietetics or related field, or bachelor’s degree if licensed prior to 2024 (required)

• Registered Dietitian credentialed through the Commission on Dietetic Registration (required)

• State licensure or certification as required for practice

• 2+ years of experience as a Registered Dietitian, with experience in eating disorder treatment (required)

• Experience in PHP, IOP, residential, or inpatient setting (preferred)

Skills and Approach (preferred)

• Practices from a weight-inclusive framework

• Adopts an "all foods fit" approach toward clinical nutrition

• Comfortable providing nutrition care in a behavioral treatment context, where the meal plan is an exposure rather than only a prescription

• Able to hold the meal plan under patient distress without negotiating, accommodating, or reassuring

• Recognizes how co-occurring OCD, trauma, and mood symptoms present around food, and adjusts approach accordingly

• Comfortable with medical acuity and with escalating medical concerns promptly

• Works within a defined curriculum and fidelity expectations rather than an idiosyncratic model

• Practices as an independent clinical discipline and collaborates with therapists as peers

• Seeks and uses supervision and consultation

We know job descriptions can be intimidating, so if this sounds like an opportunity for you, please don't hesitate to apply!

Who We Are

Compass Health Center is a recognized leader in crisis-level mental health, bringing passion, connection, and patient-centered care to the Partial Hospitalization and Intensive Outpatient space (PHP/IOP). Based in Chicagoland, we serve hundreds of patients every day, ranging from ages 5 through adulthood, in our onsite facilities or through our flourishing virtual programming. Compass fills a critical gap between outpatient and inpatient care through an intermediate level of Behavioral Healthcare.

A few more things we want you to know: our values are super important to us, and hopefully will be to you, too. Cultural humility, teamwork, continuous improvement, connection, patient centered care, passion, innovation, and agility should be your power sources. Joining Compass is an opportunity to feel fulfilled through a joint mission towards healing our communities.

Benefits & Perks

We know that you will be dedicated to your purpose here. We look at that investment as a two-way street. We are proud to offer plenty of space for growth, and opportunities to pursue continuous development within our organization.

For eligible positions, our other benefits include: comprehensive medical/dental/vision plans, 401k program with company matching, generous PTO (including competitive parental leave after 1 year of employment), and continuous training through CEU seminars and volunteering opportunities.

What’s Next?

Compass is committed to cultivating diverse and dynamic teams who exude passion for their craft, so whether or not you check all the boxes, we encourage you to apply – we’d be grateful to hear from you!

jobs.title: Employee Relations Lead
jobs.location: New York, New York, United States
jobs.description:
CLEAR is building THE secure identity company of the future. Our mission is to make experiences safer and easier—physically and digitally. With more than 43 million Members and a growing network of partners across the world, CLEAR's secure identity platform is transforming the way people live, work, and travel. Whether it’s at the airport, stadium, or throughout your everyday life, CLEAR unlocks the magic of frictionless experiences.

The Employee Relations Lead serves as the centralized employee relations (ER) partner for across CLEAR’s business. In this role, you're the consistent thread ensuring employee relations issues are handled the same way, every time, no matter where they happen. You're the person leaders lean on to make good calls, and the person team members know is invested in their success. This role puts you in the middle of it all — maintaining oversight across the entire employee population  while coaching leaders, resolving employee relations issues with consistency and fairness across the field, and ensuring excellent process adherence that helps CLEAR thrive.

What you'll do:

• Own employee and labor relations across the business: run investigations, dig into root causes, and land on outcomes that are fair, defensible, and consistent, working closely with Legal along the way.

• Lead timely, thorough, and objective workplace investigations involving employee complaints, misconduct, policy violations, and other employee relations matters.

• Coach and advise leaders on corrective action, conflict resolution, policy interpretation, and consistent employment practices, so issues are addressed early and handled appropriately and consistently.

• Manage and ensure consistency in workers’ compensation, leave of absence (LOA), and accommodation cases, including reviewing claims and requests, with our Leave Administrators, Legal, and ensuring decisions align with company policy and applicable laws (e.g., FMLA, ADA, state and local leave laws).

• Support unemployment claims by reviewing separation circumstances, preparing accurate and timely responses, and ensuring documentation supports company decisions.

• Identify employee relations trends across case, claims, leave, and accommodation data, and partner with People leadership to develop proactive solutions that improve accountability, reduce risk, and strengthen the employee experience.

• Partner across People, Legal and Operations on process improvements and larger initiatives, ensuring ER, leave, accommodation, and claims practices are applied the same way at every station.

• Maintain accurate, confidential case documentation and ensure all ER decisions comply with company policies and applicable employment laws.

How you'll measure success:

• Fewer repeat employee relations issues, and faster, smarter resolution when they do come up.

• Leaders and managers putting the training and programs you build to real use.

• People processes running consistently at every station.

What you're great at:

• 5+ years of HR and Employee Relations experience, including real time supporting hourly or frontline teams and handling complex employee relations matters.

• Earning trust with operational leaders quickly, and coaching them through hard calls with good judgment and empathy.

• Reading data and what people are actually telling you, then turning both into action.

• Juggling a lot at once without losing the thread, in an environment that shifts week to week.

• Communicating clearly at every level - whether that's a one-on-one coaching conversation or a room full of station leaders.

How You'll be Rewarded:

At CLEAR, we help YOU move forward - because when you’re at your best, we’re at our best. You’ll work with talented team members motivated by our mission of making experiences safer and easier. Our offices are bright and energetic with an open concept and plenty of conference rooms and casual co-working spaces. We also offer catered lunches every day and have fully stocked kitchens. Outside of the office, we invest in your well-being and learning & development with stipends and reimbursement programs.

We offer holistic total rewards, including comprehensive healthcare plans, family-building benefits (fertility and adoption/surrogacy support), flexible time off, annual wellness stipend, free OneMedical memberships for you and your dependents, a CLEAR Plus membership, and a 401(k) retirement plan with employer match. The base salary range for this role is $100,000 - $140,000, depending on levels of skills and experience.

The base salary range represents the low and high end of CLEAR’s salary range for this position. Salaries will vary depending on various factors which include, but are not limited to location, education, skills, experience and performance. The range listed is just one component of CLEAR’s total compensation package for employees and other rewards may include annual bonuses, commission, Restricted Stock Units.

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

CLEAR provides reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals with disabilities or protected needs. Please let us know if you require a reasonable accommodation to apply for a job or perform your job. Examples of reasonable accommodation include, but are not limited to, time off, extra breaks, making a change to the application process or work procedures, policy exceptions, providing documents in an alternative format, live captioning or using a sign language interpreter, or using specialized equipment.

We are committed to a transparent and secure hiring process. All communications related to this role will come directly from a CLEAR employee through valid CLEAR channels (e.g., a valid @clearme.com email address or verified CLEAR LinkedIn profile). We encourage candidates to remain alert to job scams and to report any suspicious activity.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Technician I, MD Fill - B2 Shift
jobs.description:
This is our MD Fill - Aseptic Gown - B2 night shift:  6pm-6:30am Wednesday - Friday & every other Saturday

Performs functions associated with cGMP manufacturing operations within the biologics production facility, including working with engineers in set-up and calibration tasks, as well as performing rework and quality testing related to the production of parts, components and final materials. Uses sophisticated programs (such as LIMS, SAP, automated control systems, etc.) to collect and evaluate operating data, which can be used to conduct on-line adjustments to products, instruments or equipment. Determines and may assist in developing methods and procedures to control or modify the manufacturing process.

Responsibilities

• Must have the ability to become aseptic gown certified.
• Shipping finished materials.
• Maintaining inventory levels.
• Sampling of in process and raw materials.
• Running glass washer / autoclave.
• Buffer / media preparation.
• Equipment preparation (CIP / SIP).
• Cell culture (from vial thaw to production scale).
• Column chromatography.
• Tangential flow filtration
• Wear an aseptic gown during an 8 hr shift. This gown covers the full body.
• Willing to complete a lot cleaning sanitation during the work shift
• Follow all clean room entry and exit procedures
• Wear the required aseptic gowning and PPE correctly at all times
• Perform hand hygiene and sanitization before entering the clean room
• Maintain aseptic technique to prevent contamination of materials and products
• Sanitize work surfaces, tools, and equipment on a frequent and consistent basis
• Minimize movement, talking, and unnecessary activity in the clean room
• Inspect gowning and PPE for proper fit and integrity before use
• Report any contamination concerns, spills, or equipment issues immediately
• Handle sterile materials only in approved areas and in a controlled manner
• Follow all environmental monitoring and cleaning requirements
• Dispose of waste and contaminated materials according to procedure
• Complete all required documentation accurately and on time. Good hand writing will be a huge plus.

Please note that the YouTube video is not owned, produced, or sponsored by AbbVie and does not accurately depict AbbVie’s aseptic processes and procedures. The video is provided solely as an example of the aseptic gowning process.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rngOnQle5ew

This is our MD Fill - Aseptic Gown - B2 night shift:  6pm-6:30am Wednesday - Friday & every other Saturday

• Must have the ability to become aseptic gown certified.
• High School diploma (or equivalent experience), with 2+ years experience. Associates degree in science, with 1+ years relevant experience. Bachelor's Degree with 0+ year relevant experience.
• Aseptic experience (Preferred)
• Aseptic PPE Experience (Preferred)
• Acquires job skills and learns company policies and procedures to complete routine tasks.
• Works on assignments that are routine in nature, requiring limited judgment.
• Has the ability to recognize when accepted practices are deviated from.

jobs.description:
Galileo is looking for an experienced leader to join our team as a Camp Director. Camp Directors lead our dynamic summer camps for K–8th grade, serving as both site General Manager and the public face of the organization.

You will open and operate a Camp Galileo location serving campers and their families within your community! You will lead a dynamic seasonal team of educators as well as enthusiastic entry-level staff to create joyful, safe environments and ensure smooth daily operations. With a focus on exceptional camper and family experiences, you will uphold program quality, foster creativity, and deliver excellence in customer care, curriculum, and team leadership.

Why This Role Matters

Galileo started in 2002 with a single summer camp in Palo Alto, named for Galileo Galilei, one of history’s great innovators. Today we run 90+ sites across eight states, and Camp Directors are still the people who give each camp its own traditions and magic. Our mission is to develop innovators who envision and create a better world, and at camp, you’re the one who makes that real for campers, families, and staff every day.

You will be Accountable for

Bringing Galileo’s Spirit to Life

• Infuse camp with joy, tradition, and creativity

• Build an inclusive environment where every camper, staff member, and family feels seen, supported, and inspired

Leading with Ownership and Vision

• Own every aspect of your camp’s launch, from preseason planning through end-of-summer wrap-up

• As both operational lead and culture builder, oversee every detail from daily camp operations to parent communication while delivering an exceptional program

Keeping Camp Safe and Running Smoothly

• Prioritize camper safety, family trust, and program fidelity at all times

• Anticipate needs, adapt quickly, and problem-solve on the fly so camp runs seamlessly, even when things don’t go as planned

Developing and Managing Your Team

• Train and mentor a staff of 7 to 40 (depending on site size), including educators and entry-level staff, while actively building your team culture

• Provide clear expectations for instructional and program standards, ongoing feedback, and professional development

• Own core management responsibilities such as training support, scheduling, payroll, and ongoing performance management

Embracing Challenge and Innovation

• Use the Galileo Innovation Approach (GIA) to encourage curiosity and problem-solving

• Lead your team in turning challenges into opportunities, keeping both spirit and operations aligned to Galileo’s mission

• Communicate openly with your Field Program Manager, seek out feedback, and turn it into action

• Take ownership of your own professional development, staying self-motivated to learn, grow, and improve throughout the summer

Building Strong Partnerships

• Serve as the primary face of camp within the community

• Communicate proactively with families, facilities partners, and cross-functional teams

• Collaborate with your Field Program Manager and cultivate trust with community partners, staff, and campers

Location & Work Schedule:

This is a seasonal role running March–September 2027, with a schedule divided into three phases. Exact dates will vary based on hire date and specific site operating dates:

• Phase One: Training & Prep (March–June): 5 to 15 hours per week, depending on tenure and start date — mostly flexible and remote, with some required scheduled and in-person commitments. This phase includes in-person training(s), a Bay Area retreat, scheduled virtual training(s), marketing events, and on-site prep at your camp location during the week leading up to camp. Some events may take place during evenings and weekends.

• Phase Two: On-Site (June–August): On-site hours typically range from 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM (M-F), up to 50 hours per week over 5–8 weeks, depending on camp placement.

• Phase Three: Wrap-Up (Aug–Sept): Up to 5 hrs total, remote, for final admin tasks and staff reviews.

Compensation:

(Year 1 estimate):

• Preseason (Feb–June): Earn hourly pay ($23-25/hour) for flexible, part-time prep and training

• Camp Season (June–Aug): Transition to a weekly salary ($1,500/week, plus an additional $50/week for each year of returning tenure in this role) as a full-time, exempt Camp Director during summer operations

• Postseason (Aug–Sept): Wrap up with light part-time work, paid hourly ($23-25/hour)

• Bonus/Commission: Earn an additional $1 per camper-week enrollment, plus potential commission for add-on weeks

Exact compensation may vary and will be based on multiple factors, including geography and Galileo camp director tenure. Our pay practices are guided by a commitment to equity and informed by market benchmarking and internal audits to minimize bias and ensure fairness across all roles.

Perks:

• Free camp for your child(ren) or two giftable weeks (incl. extended care)

• 15% Friends & Family discount

• Priority nomination for financial assistance for someone you know

• 3+ years of experience working directly with students in an education setting (out-of-school time, teaching, education administration, camps/recreation, etc.) is required

• Minimum 1 year of experience managing or supervising adult staff is required

• Proven experience creating safe, inclusive environments for children and building trust with families

• Proven experience setting clear expectations, giving ongoing feedback, and coaching staff to improve

• Demonstrated ability to manage operational details like scheduling, staffing, and payroll

• Track record of staying calm and making sound decisions in fast-paced situations, including safety issues and challenging conversations with families

• Strong written and verbal communication with families, partners, and supervisors

• Experience with hands-on, project-based learning (STEAM, art, design, maker programs) is a plus

• Availability for part-time remote work starting Feb 2026, and full-time on-site work starting June 2026 (dates vary by location)

• Willingness to travel in the region to up to 3 in person marketing events, in the preseason

• Ability to complete all required training before camp begins

• Ability to meet state requirements to work with children, including mandated screenings and Adult & Child First Aid/CPR/AED certification

We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team and strongly encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds and experiences. If you think you have what it takes to be successful in this role, we encourage you to apply.

Additional Information

Please note that our job descriptions are a summary of the typical functions of the job, not an exhaustive or comprehensive list of all possible responsibilities, tasks, and duties.

We comply with the ADA and provide reasonable accommodations that allow qualified applicants/employees to perform the essential functions of the job. To request an accommodation, contact our Human Resources team.

During the onboarding process, in accordance with applicable local and state requirements, you may be required to complete a Tuberculosis (TB)

jobs.title: Senior RF Test Engineer I
jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

SENIOR RF TEST ENGINEER I

We’re currently seeking an Senior RF Test Engineer I for our global headquarters in Long Beach, CA. This team is responsible for building the tools and process to test satellite RF subsystems and our line of radio products.

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO:

• Develop RF test plans for RF subsystems and payloads.

• Manage and conduct Acceptance, Qualification and Proto-Flight test programs on RF systems.

• Design, procure and assemble automated test tools for RF subsystems.

• Support the design and development of space flight hardware to increase the level of testability and manufacturability

• Contribute to the development of engineering and business processes, including engineering and test processes, as well as other business processes to support Rocket Lab growth and capability

• Contribute to the development of engineering best practice areas such as test, design for manufacture and engineering change management.

YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering or related technical discipline

• 5+ years of experience with RF hardware development and RF testing

• U.S. citizenship is required, due to program requirements

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

• Understanding of electrical test equipment, test procedures, data acquisition systems and instrumentation

• Understanding of designing hardware from concept through production

• Experience in environmental design testing, such as vibration, shock, thermal, and TVAC

• Project/program management skills

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.

Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.

Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.

Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base Pay Range (CA Only)

$132,000—$198,000 USD

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. Learn more about ITAR here.

Rocket Lab provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment at Rocket Lab, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for the application/interview process for a job in the United States should contact Giulia Johnson at g.biow@rocketlabusa.com.This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days.

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY:

jobs.title: Revenue FP&A Director
jobs.description:
Who is Sonar?
Sonar enables organizations to ship agentic code with confidence. Code creation is abundant, but confidence is scarce. Our core platform, SonarQube, verifies over 750 billion lines of code every day, delivering agentic verification and governance for all code. Trusted by more than 7 million developers and 75% of the Fortune 100, including teams at Nvidia, ServiceNow, Booking.com, Goldman Sachs, AstraZeneca, and Ford Motor Company, Sonar enables organizations to reduce outages, improve security, and lower the cost and risk of agentic software development.

Founded in Geneva and now headquartered in Austin, Texas, Sonar has a global team working across offices and hubs, including Silicon Valley, London, Bochum, Barcelona, Singapore, Tokyo, and the Washington, D.C. area. At Sonar, we’re enabling enterprises to build agentic software factories that can move quickly while maintaining the control, consistency and evidence required to ship with confidence. 


Position description
We are seeking a Revenue Finance Director to join our FP&A team and own how Sonar forecasts, plans, and prices its revenue. You will drive forecast accuracy, partner cross-functionally to optimize revenue, and give executives clear recommendations on revenue strategy. This is a hands-on role for a self-starter who pushes back with data, builds their own solutions, and leads our AI-first approach to FP&A.
 
What you will do
Own the Revenue Forecast and Raise Its AccuracyOwn Sonar’s revenue forecast end to end (bookings, billings, and revenue) across monthly and quarter-end cycles, with a clear view of where we will land and why.Treat forecast accuracy as your personal scorecard. Track misses by segment, motion, and root cause, and run retrospectives on material variances.Challenge cross-functional teams on conversion, renewal, and timing assumptions, and drive the changes needed to make the forecast more reliable.Build driver-based models using leading indicators (pipeline, usage, renewals, price) and ASC 606 treatment; incorporating consumption based revenue models.
Lead long-range and annual revenue planning, translating targets across the P&L.
Turn analysis into executive level recommendations
Shape revenue strategy and bring a position and options to the CFO. Build Board, investor, and ELT materials.
Evaluate pricing and packaging changes (list price, discounting, renewal uplift, plan mix) and quantify the impact on topline and margin.
Partner with Deal Desk, Pricing, and R&D Finance to analyze margin, pricing profiles, and deal structures (discounts, multi-year terms, ramps, payment terms, commitments).
Build deal guardrails and approval frameworks that balance growth, margin, and revenue recognition, advise on non-standard deals, and run post-close analysis.
Build with AI and Automate
Default to AI first. Before adding a manual process, ask whether an AI-enabled workflow can do it better, and build it yourself.
Ship automations that go beyond text generation: forecast roll-ups, variance analysis, anomaly detection, deal and pricing analytics, and agentic workflows.
Define where AI should automate, where human judgment stays in the loop, and how outputs are validated, with appropriate controls and data security.
Roll Up Your Sleeves and Self-Initiate
Stay hands-on in the data and the models. Spot problems and opportunities on your own, propose the fix, and drive it to completion without waiting to be asked.
Partner with Controllership, Accounting, Finance Ops, RevOps, and Deal Desk to ensure data integrity and accurate, streamlined reporting.

Experience and qualifications
The ideal candidate will: 
Required Experience10+ years of progressive finance experience (FP&A, revenue finance, or commercial and strategic finance), with significant time in high-growth SaaS or tech.Ownership of a revenue, bookings, or ARR forecast at scale, with a proven record of improving accuracy and working knowledge of revenue accounting.A history of pricing, packaging, or commercial recommendations that executives adopted, grounded in margin, discounting, and price realization analysis.Experience with consumption based modelsDemonstrated influence: you challenge senior leaders with data, hold your position under pushback, and change how others work.Hands-on AI experience in finance workflows, with specific automations you built and shipped (not just prompts for polishing emails), using tools such as Claude or ChatGPT.Expert-level, driver-based financial modeling, and the ability to communicate complex recommendations clearly to executives, the Board, and investors.A self-starter and builder who takes ownership, moves fast, and does the detailed work personally.Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, or a related field.
Preferred QualificationsMBA, or investment banking, consulting, or strategic finance experience.Experience with various pricing models.Hands-on experience with enterprise planning and finance systems (e.g., NetSuite, Pigment, Salesforce).Experience building AI agents or workflows (e.g., Claude Cowork).

You will open and operate a Camp Galileo location serving campers and their families within your community! You will lead a dynamic seasonal team of educators as well as enthusiastic entry-level staff to create joyful, safe environments and ensure smooth daily operations. With a focus on exceptional camper and family experiences, you will uphold program quality, foster creativity, and deliver excellence in customer care, curriculum, and team leadership.

Why This Role Matters

Galileo started in 2002 with a single summer camp in Palo Alto, named for Galileo Galilei, one of history’s great innovators. Today we run 90+ sites across eight states, and Camp Directors are still the people who give each camp its own traditions and magic. Our mission is to develop innovators who envision and create a better world, and at camp, you’re the one who makes that real for campers, families, and staff every day.

You will be Accountable for

Bringing Galileo’s Spirit to Life

• Infuse camp with joy, tradition, and creativity

• Build an inclusive environment where every camper, staff member, and family feels seen, supported, and inspired

Leading with Ownership and Vision

• Own every aspect of your camp’s launch, from preseason planning through end-of-summer wrap-up

• As both operational lead and culture builder, oversee every detail from daily camp operations to parent communication while delivering an exceptional program

Keeping Camp Safe and Running Smoothly

• Prioritize camper safety, family trust, and program fidelity at all times

• Anticipate needs, adapt quickly, and problem-solve on the fly so camp runs seamlessly, even when things don’t go as planned

Developing and Managing Your Team

• Train and mentor a staff of 7 to 40 (depending on site size), including educators and entry-level staff, while actively building your team culture

• Provide clear expectations for instructional and program standards, ongoing feedback, and professional development

• Own core management responsibilities such as training support, scheduling, payroll, and ongoing performance management

Embracing Challenge and Innovation

• Use the Galileo Innovation Approach (GIA) to encourage curiosity and problem-solving

• Lead your team in turning challenges into opportunities, keeping both spirit and operations aligned to Galileo’s mission

• Communicate openly with your Field Program Manager, seek out feedback, and turn it into action

• Take ownership of your own professional development, staying self-motivated to learn, grow, and improve throughout the summer

Building Strong Partnerships

• Serve as the primary face of camp within the community

• Communicate proactively with families, facilities partners, and cross-functional teams

• Collaborate with your Field Program Manager and cultivate trust with community partners, staff, and campers

Location & Work Schedule:

This is a seasonal role running March–September 2027, with a schedule divided into three phases. Exact dates will vary based on hire date and specific site operating dates:

• Phase One: Training & Prep (March–June): 5 to 15 hours per week, depending on tenure and start date — mostly flexible and remote, with some required scheduled and in-person commitments. This phase includes in-person training(s), a Bay Area retreat, scheduled virtual training(s), marketing events, and on-site prep at your camp location during the week leading up to camp. Some events may take place during evenings and weekends.

• Phase Two: On-Site (June–August): On-site hours typically range from 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM (M-F), up to 50 hours per week over 5–8 weeks, depending on camp placement.

• Phase Three: Wrap-Up (Aug–Sept): Up to 5 hrs total, remote, for final admin tasks and staff reviews.

Compensation:

(Year 1 estimate):

• Preseason (Feb–June): Earn hourly pay ($22-24/hour) for flexible, part-time prep and training

• Camp Season (June–Aug): Transition to a weekly salary ($1,400/week plus an additional $50/week for each year of returning tenure in this role) as a full-time, exempt Camp Director during summer operations

• Postseason (Aug–Sept): Wrap up with light part-time work, paid hourly ($22-24/hour)

• Bonus/Commission: Earn an additional $1 per camper-week enrollment, plus potential commission for add-on weeks

Exact compensation may vary and will be based on multiple factors, including geography and Galileo camp director tenure. Our pay practices are guided by a commitment to equity and informed by market benchmarking and internal audits to minimize bias and ensure fairness across all roles.

Perks:

• Free camp for your child(ren) or two giftable weeks (incl. extended care)

• 15% Friends & Family discount

• Priority nomination for financial assistance for someone you know

• 3+ years of experience working directly with students in an education setting (out-of-school time, teaching, education administration, camps/recreation, etc.) is required

• Minimum 1 year of experience managing or supervising adult staff is required

• Proven experience creating safe, inclusive environments for children and building trust with families

• Proven experience setting clear expectations, giving ongoing feedback, and coaching staff to improve

• Demonstrated ability to manage operational details like scheduling, staffing, and payroll

• Track record of staying calm and making sound decisions in fast-paced situations, including safety issues and challenging conversations with families

• Strong written and verbal communication with families, partners, and supervisors

• Experience with hands-on, project-based learning (STEAM, art, design, maker programs) is a plus

• Availability for part-time remote work starting Feb 2026, and full-time on-site work starting June 2026 (dates vary by location)

• Willingness to travel in the region to up to 3 in person marketing events, in the preseason

• Ability to complete all required training before camp begins

• Ability to meet state requirements to work with children, including mandated screenings and Adult & Child First Aid/CPR/AED certification

We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team and strongly encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds and experiences. If you think you have what it takes to be successful in this role, we encourage you to apply.

Additional Information

Please note that our job descriptions are a summary of the typical functions of the job, not an exhaustive or comprehensive list of all possible responsibilities, tasks, and duties.

We comply with the ADA and provide reasonable accommodations that allow qualified applicants/employees to perform the essential functions of the job. To request an accommodation, contact our Human Resources team.

During the onboarding process, in accordance with applicable local and state requirements, you may be required to complete a Tuberculosis (TB)

What You'll Earn

jobs.title: Account Executive - Engineering Firms (California)
jobs.description:
ABOUT CIVILGRID

CivilGrid is the trusted civil design platform powering affordable infrastructure renewal and growth. We give utilities, civil engineers, and municipalities a single, collaborative source of truth for what's underground so teams can plan, design, and build faster, smarter, and safer.



Our platform consolidates utility records, geotechnical and environmental data, paving moratoriums, and jurisdictional requirements directly from 3,000+ utilities, agencies, and municipalities with full chain-of-custody documentation. Teams at PG&E, Mark Thomas, and dozens of leading engineering firms use CivilGrid to cut research time by up to 88%, reduce project costs, prevent dig-ins, and accelerate delivery on the projects that keep communities running.



We’re a venture-backed Series A startup tackling a $4.7T US infrastructure market that has been underserved by software for decades. Founded by industry insiders, each with 10+ years in utilities and civil engineering, we move fast, ship work that matters, and stay close to the customers and field teams we build for.



WHY THIS ROLE

We’re seeking a highly motivated and outcomes-driven Account Executive to own and grow CivilGrid’s presence across civil engineering and design firms in the US West. The ideal candidate has a proven track record of enterprise sales success within the AEC (architecture, engineering, and construction) sector, and brings creativity and persistence to every stage of the sales process.



This role is purpose-built for a seller who understands how engineering firms operate — from project kickoffs and utility research workflows to survey and SUE coordination, CAD/GIS deliverables, and firm-level capacity constraints. You’ll be helping mid-to-large civil engineering firms cut weeks of manual records research, eliminate rework, and deliver better-quality designs faster with CivilGrid’s civil design platform.



This role reports into our Director of Sales and is specifically focused on civil engineering and design firms in the US West. It is a remote role, but you must be based in California to be considered.



WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Deliver and exceed sales targets with a strong, quantifiable history of success

Lead complex enterprise sales cycles from prospecting through contract execution, including:

 - Securing sponsorship across regional directors, discipline leads, and firm-level operations leadership

 - Running pilots with clear success criteria tied to engineering KPIs (records research time, rework incidents, data request turnaround)

 - Converting pilots into firm-wide enterprise contracts covering multiple offices and project teams

 - Develop creative, targeted outbound campaigns tailored to engineering firm buyer personas — Regional Directors, Project Managers, Civil Engineers, Survey/SUE Leads, and GIS Technicians

 - Navigate AEC firm procurement processes, including IT security reviews, compliance, and vendor onboarding requirements

 - Build compelling sales materials including executive presentations, ROI analyses, and business cases demonstrating measurable impact on research time, cost per project, and field safety

 - Maintain stakeholder engagement throughout enterprise sales cycles, with strategies to align with firm growth initiatives, new contract wins, and project pipeline timing

 - Represent CivilGrid at AEC, civil engineering, and infrastructure industry conferences with a strategic, outcome-focused approach to networking and prospecting

 - Leverage and expand an existing personal network in the civil engineering and AEC space to open new opportunities and drive pipeline growth



WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - 5+ years of enterprise sales experience with a strong record of hitting or exceeding quota

 - Experience selling construction-tech, GIS software, or similar to engineering firms is a must

 - Deep understanding of how engineering firms evaluate and buy technology: workflow pain points, project manager influence, firm-wide rollout challenges, and billable-hour impact

 - Excellent communication skills with the ability to adapt messaging for firm leadership, technical engineers, and operational stakeholders

 - Highly competitive, driven, and outcome-oriented

 - Excellent at forecasting accurately quarter over quarter

 - Proven ability to manage multi-threaded deals with sales cycles spanning project managers, discipline directors, GIS/IT teams, and firm leadership

 - Excellent at using all the different sales platforms such, SFDC, Gong, Zoominfo, Salesloft or outreach, etc.

 - Based in California



BONUS POINTS

 - Prior experience selling GIS, CAD, project management, or data research software to AEC firms

 - Existing relationships at mid-to-large civil engineering or design firms in the US West

 - Familiarity with utility record request workflows, SUE (subsurface utility engineering), or design data management

 - Experience selling into multi-office AEC firms where deals require coordination across regional leadership and firm-wide IT approvals



HOW WE WORK

We’re a small, but rapidly growing team that ships. Expect direct feedback, real ownership from day one, and proximity to customers — huge utilities, public agencies, and engineering firms whose work depends on what we build. We default to in-person collaboration where it matters and remote-friendly flexibility otherwise. We hire people who care deeply about their craft and the communities our customers serve.



COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

The base salary range for this role is $119,000 - $150,000. This role has a 50/50 base to commission split, bringing total OTE to $238,000 - $300,000.



Cash is only one part of your total compensation package at CivilGrid, which also includes meaningful early-stage equity, comprehensive benefits, and the opportunity to shape a category-defining company. jobs.title: Senior Harness Design Engineer II
jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

SENIOR HARNESS DESIGN ENGINEER II

Based out of Rocket Lab's global headquarters in Long Beach, CA, the Senior Harness Design Engineer II will primarily focus on the design, development, and integration of electrical harnesses for our spacecraft. This includes defining interfaces, selecting components, specifying split locations and lengths, and generating design documentation to support the spacecraft engineering team. The Harness Design Engineer will also collaborate with systems engineering, mechanical engineering, and assembly, integration, and test (AIT) teams to ensure seamless integration of harness systems into our spacecraft.

This role emphasizes electrical engineering principles, including wiring diagram development, interface definition, and electrical system architecture interpretation, while supporting the full lifecycle of harness engineering from design to fabrication and integration.

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO:

• Harnessing responsibilities:

• Design and develop electrical harness systems for spacecraft, including connector and backshell selection, wire selection, shielding, and routing.

• Generate wiring diagrams, pinout tables, and interface definitions for harness systems based on spacecraft interconnect diagrams.

• Collaborate with systems engineering to interpret system architecture and define electrical interfaces.

• Create and maintain Bills of Materials (BOMs) for harness systems in the product lifecycle management (PLM) tool.

• Develop and maintain fabrication drawings and documentation for harness systems using tools such as Capital Essentials, NX, and Teamcenter.

• Support harness fabrication processes, ensuring compliance with space-grade standards and industry best practices.

• Define and verify harness acceptance criteria, including electrical testing and inspection.

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams (e.g., systems engineering, mechanical engineering, and AIT) to ensure proper integration of harnesses into spacecraft.

• Electrical Engineering responsibilities:

• Perform electrical design and analysis to ensure harness systems meet performance, reliability, and manufacturability requirements.

• Support electrical system schematics and harness design documentation.

• Participate in design reviews, providing technical input and ensuring harness designs meet program requirements.

• Troubleshoot and resolve electrical issues related to harness systems during fabrication, integration, and testing.

YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS AS A SENIOR HARNESS DESIGN ENGINEER II:

• Bachelor’s degree in aerospace, mechanical, or electrical engineering; or other engineering degree

• 8+ years of electrical engineering or avionics experience

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

• Master’s or PhD in aerospace, mechanical, or electrical engineering; or other engineering degree

• Experience in the aerospace/defense industry

• Experience supporting satellite development programs and satellite operations

• Proficiency in electrical engineering principles, including power distribution, signal integrity, grounding, and communication systems (e.g., RS-422, SPI, Ethernet, CAN bus).

• Experience with harness design tools such as Capital Essentials, NX, and Teamcenter.

• Familiarity with industry standards for harness design and fabrication (e.g., NASA-STD-8739.4, IPC/WHMA-A-620).

• Experience with electrical testing of harness systems, including continuity testing, insulation resistance testing, and functional testing.

• Knowledge of thermal and mechanical considerations for harness routing and integration.

• Familiarity with requirement management tools such as JAMA.

• Ability to work in a dynamic environment with competing priorities.

• Ability to obtain a Top Secret Clearance

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.

Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.

Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.

Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base Pay Range (CA Only)

$151,500—$252,500 USD

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

Important information:

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY:

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. Learn more about ITAR here.

Rocket Lab provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment at Rocket Lab, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for the application/interview process for a job in the United States should contact Giulia Johnson at g.biow@rocketlabusa.com.This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days.

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY:

For security reasons, background checks will be undertaken prior to any employment offers being made to an applicant.  These checks will include nationality checks as it is a requirement of this position that you be eligible to access equipment and data regulated by the United States' International Traffic in Arms Regulations.

jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager, Fragrance
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE AT OSMO:

Osmo is the Olfactory Intelligence company, on a mission to give AI a sense of smell to improve the health and wellbeing of human life. Why? Our sense of smell has the ability to delight us, protect us, and heal us.

Olfactory Intelligence has applications across industries including fragrance, manufacturing, security, medicine, and more. We believe in the power of automation and thoughtfully applied AI/ML to solve problems beyond the reach of human intuition alone.



We're headquartered in Elizabeth, NJ, with an additional office in Somerville, MA. We provide complimentary shuttle service from Brooklyn and Newark, NJ.



ABOUT THE ROLE:

As Senior Technical Program Manager, you will lead program management for Fragrance House and report to the SVP of Product Management. You own the plan, schedule, metrics, and risks for a portfolio that spans the software platform and AI tools that run the business, programs for enterprise and direct customers, new product launches, and manufacturing in house and with contract manufacturers. You start with the platform, working with product and engineering to define and ship it, then own how it connects to the lab, manufacturing, and shipping so the tools match how the work is done. 



You also own the path from signed order or customer brief to product that arrives on the committed date and meets specification. You do not manage the teams you work across, so you lead through written plans, data, and the curiosity to understand each team's real constraints. Tenacity keeps programs moving when demand exceeds capacity, and kindness keeps the trade-offs you push back on from costing you trust.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Own the Portfolio — Run the Fragrance House program portfolio, including intake, scoping, and prioritization of new programs as the business adds customers, products, and capabilities.

 - Ship the Platform — Partner with product management and engineering to plan and deliver the software platform and AI tools that run Fragrance House, from requirements through launch.

 - Roll Out Tools to Operations — Lead the rollout of new software and AI tools into lab and manufacturing operations, including training, adoption tracking, and the feedback loop to engineering.

 - Connect Software to Physical Work — Map where software and physical processes meet, automate the manual steps that cause delay or error against a baseline, and make sure data created in physical work (formulas, batch records, quality results) reaches the systems and models that depend on it.

 - Own Order to Delivery — Own the process from signed order or customer brief through formulation, sampling, production, quality release, and shipment, and set the service level and metric for each handoff.

 - Govern Program Metrics — Define objectives, scope, milestones, and metrics for each program, and run KPI reporting across the portfolio for on-time delivery, brief turnaround time, tool adoption, quality, and cost to serve.

 - Run the Operating Cadence — Lead weekly business reviews, quarterly planning, and inputs to the annual operating plan for Fragrance House.

 - Manage Dependencies — Coordinate across the teams that support Fragrance House and set priority order with them when demand exceeds capacity.

 - Surface Risk Early — Identify risks before they block delivery, document mitigation plans, and escalate trade-offs with a clear recommendation.

 - Make It Repeatable — Document standard operating procedures so each program can repeat across customers and product categories.

 


WHO YOU ARE:

 - 5+ Years in Program or Project Management — You have a sustained track record running programs, not a single stretch of project coordination.

 - Software and AI Delivery — You have delivered software or AI products with engineering teams, from requirements through launch.

 - Software Meets Physical Operations — You have delivered programs that connect software systems to manufacturing, lab work, or supply chain.

 - Strategy Through Delivery — You have owned program strategy and end to end delivery, and you communicate results clearly to senior leadership.

 - Data-Driven — You use data and metrics to decide what to fix and to prove that the fix worked.

 - Cross-Functional Leader Without Authority — You work across technical and non-technical teams, and you set priorities and resolve conflicts through written plans and data rather than reporting lines.

 - Curious and Kind Under Pressure — You ask real questions about how each team works, and you push back on trade-offs with respect so people keep bringing you problems early.

 - Education — Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, chemistry, business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

 - On Site in Elizabeth, NJ — 5 days in office, or hybrid at 3 days in office.

 


WAYS TO STAND OUT:

 - AI, ML, or Data Platform Background — You have worked at a company building AI, machine learning, or data platforms.

 - New Product and Market Launches — You have led programs through the launch of new products, categories, or markets.

 - Order to Delivery Ownership — You have owned an order to delivery process across commercial, operations, and logistics teams.

 - Enterprise Delivery Commitments — You have managed programs for enterprise customers with contracted delivery dates.

jobs.title: Controller
jobs.description:
North 40 Outfitters is looking for a Controller to join our Home Office team in Great Falls, MT. We believe that each team member plays a vital role in the success of our company. We are looking for authentic and enthusiastic people who love our lifestyle and believe in service before self.

As the Controller at North 40 Outfitters, you will lead the day-to-day accounting function and play a key role in maintaining the integrity, accuracy, and effectiveness of our financial operations. You will oversee financial close and reporting, general ledger activity, inventory accounting, cash management, accounts payable and receivable, fixed assets, tax compliance, audits, and internal controls across our multi-location retail organization. This role serves as an important financial partner to company leadership and store operations, requiring strong accounting expertise, sound judgment, and an understanding of the operational realities of a high-volume retail environment.

This full-time position requires the ability to work all scheduled shifts between the business hours of Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Schedule flexibility is required based on business needs and may include periodic travel to North 40 locations or other business sites.

• Demonstrated commitment to maintaining accuracy, integrity, confidentiality, and strong financial controls.
• Self-motivated and dependable leader with the ability to take initiative, manage competing priorities, and make sound decisions.
• Strong understanding of accounting principles, GAAP, financial controls, and sound accounting practices.
• Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a closely related field.
• Significant progressive accounting experience, including financial close, general ledger, reconciliations, financial reporting, and internal controls.
• Experience leading accounting operations within a retail, multi-location, inventory-intensive, or high-transaction-volume environment strongly preferred.
• Experience overseeing monthly, quarterly, and annual financial close processes and producing accurate, timely financial statements.
• Experience maintaining accounting policies, reconciliations, documentation, approval controls, and segregation of duties.
• Strong understanding of inventory accounting, cost of goods sold, gross margin, and the financial reporting requirements of a retail organization.
• Experience overseeing cash accounting, bank reconciliations, store deposits, ACH transactions, checks, wire transfers, and other disbursements.
• Experience with cash-flow forecasting, treasury management, and monitoring banking activity for unusual or unauthorized transactions.
• Experience maintaining fixed-asset records and ensuring appropriate capitalization and depreciation of buildings, equipment, technology, vehicles, fixtures, and leasehold improvements.
• Experience tracking capital expenditures and projects from approval through completion and reconciling expenditures against approved budgets.
• Experience coordinating sales and use tax preparation, reconciliation, and filing, as well as supporting federal, state, and local tax compliance.
• Experience coordinating financial statement audits and responding to external reviews, tax audits, or governmental inquiries.
• Demonstrated ability to develop, document, implement, and continuously improve internal financial controls, segregation of duties, and approval authorities.
• Ability to establish appropriate financial controls for decentralized, multi-location retail operations and conduct periodic reviews of financial processes.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify trends, variances, anomalies, and potential errors and provide meaningful recommendations to leadership.
• Strong leadership skills with the ability to lead, develop, and hold accounting team members accountable to clear responsibilities, deadlines, controls, and performance expectations.
• Ability to develop cross-training and succession plans for critical accounting functions.
• Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills with the ability to build productive working relationships with store leadership, Operations, Merchandising, Human Resources, IT, Loss Prevention, Supply Chain, and executive leadership.
• Experience with ERP systems; Microsoft Dynamics 365 experience preferred.
• CPA or CMA designation preferred but not required.
• Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment when handling proprietary, employee, customer, banking, and financial information.
• Ability to travel periodically to North 40 locations or other business sites as needed.

BENEFITS & COMPENSATION

We offer a competitive wage, a rewarding work environment, and generous benefits and perks such as paid holidays, a 401(k) option, Health Savings Accounts (HSAs), medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, and a phenomenal employee discount on all products North 40 sells.

North 40 Outfitters is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager II - Advanced RF Systems
jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets - we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft and precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, including solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration and in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or vertically integrated components that help missions get to space, our world-class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions

SENIOR TECHNICAL PROGRAM MANAGER II, ADVANCED RF SYSTEMS

Based at Rocket Lab's global headquarters in Long Beach, CA, you are the program authority for our next-generation RF systems and payloads. You own the technical roadmap and strategic program decisions from the first “blank sheet” prototype, through flight qualification, and into high-rate production. This is a high-ownership role: you'll immerse yourself in the operational realities of National Security, civil, and commercial pioneers to turn their hardest problems into concrete technical milestones, and you'll be the person the program runs on.

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO:

• Command the Lifecycle: Build and lead the team that takes RF payloads, transponders, SAR, and communications systems from a “blank sheet” concept through qualification, high-rate production, and flight, and own the technical roadmap that grows the team's core capabilities.

• Lead the Team of Teams: Run multiple active programs at once, make sound architectural calls with Chief Engineers, navigate the hardest trade-offs in phased arrays, digital signal processing, and high-rate manufacturing, and personally dive into the most program-threatening problems alongside the team.

• Build the Bench: Grow a culture where strong people take smart, healthy risks and the best idea wins, no matter who it comes from, we back bold calls and treat an intelligent miss as the cost of moving fast and coach and develop the next generation of program and team leaders.

• Forge the Supply Chain: Manage high-stakes subcontracts and suppliers as strategic partners essential to the mission, protecting schedule and margin.

• Unblock Excellence: Synchronize cross-functional teams across hardware, software, and spectrum management and clear roadblocks quickly so the team keeps moving at speed and quality stays high.

• Influence the Future: Serve as the primary point of contact for assigned National Security, civil, and commercial customers, and partner with BD & Strategy on proposals and technical narratives that define the next generation of RF systems and payloads.

YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree in physics, math, science, or other technical discipline

• 8+ years of aerospace program management experience

• A demonstrated track record of owning a technical program, product, or team end to end and carrying it across the finish line under real pressure — we hire on what you've shipped, not years logged

• Evidence you've moved real hardware and software from prototype toward scalable, flight-ready production

• Understanding of the nuances of transponders, SAR, or advanced communication systems

• Experience identifying technical, schedule, or supply-chain risk and neutralizing it before it impacts the mission

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

• Production Velocity: A proven playbook for transitioning low-volume prototypes into high-rate production without sacrificing mission reliability.

• Domain Authority: Deep experience navigating National Security Space (NSS) or massive commercial telecommunications constellation architectures.

• Capture & Customer: Demonstrated success negotiating, capturing, and executing large U.S. Government or major commercial contracts.

• Advanced Technical Credibility: A Master's degree in Engineering or a related field that lets you peer-review technical roadmaps.

• Systems & Toolchain Fluency: You speak Systems Engineering, trade studies, interface control, requirement integrity and use Jira, Confluence, and ERP to keep program health visible at speed.

• Depth of Reps: Multiple program cycles or 8+ years in aerospace/defense sharpen the edge, but we weight the hardest thing you've shipped over the count.

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.

Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.

Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.

Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base Pay Range (CA Only)

$153,000—$229,500 USD

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

Important information:

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY:

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. Learn more about ITAR here.

Rocket Lab provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment at Rocket Lab, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for the application/interview process for a job in the United States should contact Giulia Johnson at g.biow@rocketlabusa.com.This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days.

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY:

For security reasons, background checks will be undertaken prior to any employment offers being made to an applicant.  These checks will include nationality checks as it is a requirement of this position that you be eligible to access equipment and data regulated by the United States' International Traffic in Arms Regulations.

Under these Regulations, you may be ineligible for this role if you do not hold citizenship of Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, the European Union, or a country that is part of NATO, or if you hold ineligible dual citizenship or nationality.  For more information on these Regulations, click here ITAR Regulations.
